Franz Beckenbauer has died. He passed away on **January 7, 2024**, at the age of 78, in Salzburg, Austria. His family announced his death the following day, on January 8.

Beckenbauer, nicknamed "Der Kaiser" (The Emperor), is widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of all time. His major achievements include:

- Winning the FIFA World Cup as captain of West Germany in **1974**
- Winning the World Cup again as Germany's manager in **1990**, making him one of only a few people to win the tournament both as a player and as a coach
- Winning the European Championship in **1972**
- Winning the Ballon d'Or twice (1972 and 1976)
- Winning three consecutive European Cups with Bayern Munic…

2024-01-death-oliver.r:
Christian Oliver died on **January 4, 2024**, at the age of 51.

He was killed in a **plane crash in the Caribbean**. He was traveling in a small single-engine plane that had just taken off from J.F. Mitchell Airport on the island of Bequia (part of St. Vincent and the Grenadines), bound for St. Lucia, when it crashed into the sea shortly after takeoff, near the island of Petit Nevis.

Tragically, his two young daughters, Madita (12) and Annik (10), were also killed in the crash, along with the pilot, Robert Sachs. Reports indicated the pilot had radioed about experiencing trouble and was attempting to turn back before the plane went down.

Oliver was a German-born actor whose credits includ…

2024-01-death-zagallo.r:
Mário Zagallo has died. He passed away on **January 5, 2024**, in Rio de Janeiro, at the age of 92. He had been dealing with various health problems in his later years, and his death was attributed to multiple organ failure.

Zagallo was one of the most decorated figures in football history:
- **As a player**, he won the FIFA World Cup with Brazil in 1958 and 1962
- **As a head coach**, he led Brazil to the 1970 World Cup title, making him the first person ever to win the tournament as both a player and a manager
- He also won the 1994 World Cup as an assistant coach

He remains a towering figure in Brazilian football and is remembered as one of the key architects of Brazil's footballing ide…

2024-02-death-brehme.r:
Andreas Brehme has died. He passed away on **February 20, 2024**, at the age of 63. According to reports, he suffered a cardiac arrest at his home in Munich.

His death came just weeks after the passing of his 1990 World Cup-winning teammate and then-coach Franz Beckenbauer, who died in January 2024. Brehme is best remembered for converting the 85th-minute penalty that gave West Germany a 1–0 victory over Argentina in the 1990 World Cup final in Rome, as well as for his successful club career with 1. FC Kaiserslautern, Bayern Munich, and Inter Milan.

2024-01-death-musser.r:
Alec Musser has died. He passed away on **January 12, 2024**, at his home in Del Mar, California, at the age of 50.

His death was confirmed by family members and his fiancée, Paige Press, who paid tribute to him publicly. Adam Sandler, who worked with him on *Grown Ups* (2010), also shared a tribute, remembering him as a funny, kind person. According to reports citing the San Diego County Medical Examiner's Office, his death was ruled a suicide.

Musser was best known for playing Del Henry on the soap opera *All My Children* and for his role in *Grown Ups*, as well as his work as a fitness model.

2024-01-death-soul.r:
David Soul died on **January 4, 2024**, at the age of 80. He passed away in London, where he had lived for many years (he became a British citizen in 2004). His wife, Helen Snell, announced his death, saying he died after a "valiant battle for life" surrounded by family.

Soul was born on August 28, 1943, in Chicago, and was best known for playing Detective Ken "Hutch" Hutchinson opposite Paul Michael Glaser in *Starsky & Hutch* (1975–1979). He also had a successful singing career, most notably with the 1977 number-one hit "Don't Give Up on Us," and appeared in projects such as *Salem's Lot* (1979) and numerous British stage and television productions later in life.

2024-01-office-drcongo.r:
**Félix Tshisekedi** was sworn in for a second term as president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo on **January 20, 2024**, following the presidential election held on December 20, 2023.

According to the country's electoral commission (CENI), Tshisekedi won re-election with roughly 73% of the vote, defeating challengers including Moïse Katumbi and Martin Fayulu. The results were upheld by the Constitutional Court, though opposition candidates rejected the outcome, alleging widespread irregularities and calling for the election to be annulled. The inauguration ceremony took place at the Stade des Martyrs in Kinshasa.

Tshisekedi, who leads the Union for Democracy and Social Progress (U…

2024-01-office-bhutan.r:
**Tshering Tobgay** took office as Prime Minister of Bhutan following the country's most recent National Assembly elections, held in two rounds in November 2023 and January 2024.

His party, the People's Democratic Party (PDP), won the election, and he was sworn in on January 28, 2024. This marked his second, non-consecutive term as prime minister—he had previously held the office from 2013 to 2018. He succeeded Lotay Tshering of the Druk Nyamrup Tshogpa party, who had served as prime minister since 2018.

If there have been elections or political developments in Bhutan since my knowledge was last updated, I'd recommend verifying with a current news source.

2024-02-death-tobykeith.r:
Toby Keith has died. He passed away on **February 5, 2024**, at the age of 62. He had been battling stomach cancer, which he was diagnosed with in late 2021 and publicly revealed in June 2022. He died in Oklahoma, surrounded by his family.

Keith was one of country music's biggest stars, known for hits like "Should've Been a Cowboy," "Courtesy of the Red, White and Blue," "Red Solo Cup," and "Beer for My Horses." Over his career, he sold more than 40 million albums and had dozens of chart-topping singles. He was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame shortly after his death in 2024.

2024-02-death-navalny.r:
Alexei Navalny died on **February 16, 2024**. He was 47 years old.

He died at the IK-3 "Polar Wolf" penal colony in Kharp, in Russia's Yamalo-Nenets region above the Arctic Circle, where he was serving a 19-year sentence on extremism charges that were widely regarded as politically motivated. Russian prison authorities said he felt unwell after a walk and lost consciousness, and they later attributed his death to natural causes.

His death prompted international condemnation, with many Western leaders and his supporters holding Vladimir Putin and the Russian government responsible. Navalny had previously survived a Novichok nerve agent poisoning in August 2020 and was arrested upon returnin…

2024-02-death-kiptum.r:
Kelvin Kiptum has died. He was killed in a car accident on **February 11, 2024**, at the age of 24.

**Details of the accident:**
- The crash occurred late at night (around 11 PM local time) on the road between Eldoret and Kaptagat in western Kenya, near where he trained.
- Kiptum was driving a Toyota Premio when the vehicle veered off the road and struck a tree.
- His coach, Gervais Hakizimana of Rwanda, also died in the crash. A third passenger, Sharon Kosgei, survived with injuries.

**Context on his career:**
Kiptum set the marathon world record of **2:00:35** at the Chicago Marathon in October 2023, breaking Eliud Kipchoge's previous record. Remarkably, he won all three marathons he eve…

2024-02-office-indonesia.r:
**Prabowo Subianto** won the most recent Indonesian presidential election, held on February 14, 2024.

Key details:
- He won in the first round with approximately 58.6% of the vote, avoiding a runoff
- His running mate was **Gibran Rakabuming Raka**, the son of outgoing President Joko Widodo (Jokowi)
- He defeated Anies Baswedan (about 25%) and Ganjar Pranowo (about 16%)
- This was Prabowo's third presidential bid, having lost to Jokowi in 2014 and 2019
- He was inaugurated as Indonesia's eighth president on **October 20, 2024**

Prabowo, a former special forces commander and defense minister under Jokowi, succeeded Jokowi, who was term-limited after serving two five-year terms.

2024-02-death-chao.r:
Angela Chao, CEO of Foremost Group, has died. She passed away on February 12, 2024, at the age of 50.

According to reports, she died in a car accident when her vehicle went into a pond on a private ranch in Johnson City, Texas, near Austin. Emergency responders attempted to rescue her, but she was pronounced dead at the scene. The Blanco County Sheriff's Office investigated the incident.

Angela Chao was the youngest daughter of James S.C. Chao, founder of the New York-based shipping company Foremost Group. She was also the sister of Elaine Chao, who served as U.S. Secretary of Transportation and is married to Senator Mitch McConnell. Angela became CEO of Foremost Group in 2018 and was a gr…

**Bernardo Arévalo** is the president of Guatemala who took office under those circumstances. He was sworn in just after midnight on January 15, 2024—hours later than the scheduled January 14 inauguration—after winning the August 2023 runoff election against Sandra Torres.

Key context about the contentious transition:

- Arévalo, a sociologist and former diplomat running with the Semilla (Seed) Movement party, rose from near-zero polling numbers to win on an anti-corruption platform, which alarmed Guatemala's political establishment.
- Following his victory, the Attorney General's office under Consuelo Porras pursued various legal maneuvers widely seen as attempts to overturn the results or…

2024-02-death-weathers.r:
Carl Weathers has died. He passed away on February 1, 2024, at the age of 76. According to a statement from his family, he died peacefully in his sleep at his home in Los Angeles. His death certificate later listed the cause as atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

Weathers had a long and varied career. Beyond his iconic role as Apollo Creed in the first four *Rocky* films (1976–1985), he was known for roles in *Predator* (1987), *Action Jackson* (1988), *Happy Gilmore* (1996), and more recently as Greef Karga in the Star Wars series *The Mandalorian*, for which he received an Emmy nomination. Before acting, he played professional football as a linebacker for the Oakland Raiders and in th…

2024-03-death-gossett.r:
Louis Gossett Jr. died on March 29, 2024, in Santa Monica, California. He was 87 years old.

Gossett had a long and acclaimed career. He was the first Black man to win the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor, for his role as Gunnery Sergeant Emil Foley in *An Officer and a Gentleman* (1982). He also won an Emmy for his role as Fiddler in the landmark 1977 miniseries *Roots*, and he remained active into his later years, with notable appearances in HBO's *Watchmen* (2019) and the 2023 musical film adaptation of *The Color Purple*, one of his final roles.

No, Ronna McDaniel is no longer the chair of the Republican National Committee. She stepped down on March 8, 2024, after leading the RNC since 2017.

Whatley was endorsed by Donald Trump, who pushed for new leadership at the RNC after securing the Republican presidential nomination in early 2024. At the same RNC meeting in Houston, **Lara Trump**, Donald Trump's daughter-in-law, was elected as co-chair.

**Why he left:** His resignation came one day after a lawsuit was filed by Janel Grant, a former WWE employee, who accused McMahon of sexual assault, abuse, and sex trafficking during her time at the company. The suit contained graphic allegations and also named former WWE executive John Laurinaitis. 2024-03-death-kahneman.r:
Daniel Kahneman has died. He passed away on **March 27, 2024**, at the age of 90.

Kahneman was born on March 5, 1934, in Tel Aviv and spent part of his childhood in Nazi-occupied France before emigrating to Israel. He was awarded the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2002 for his groundbreaking work on judgment and decision-making under uncertainty, much of it conducted in collaboration with Amos Tversky. His 2011 bestseller *Thinking, Fast and Slow* brought his research on cognitive biases and the dual-system model of thinking (fast, intuitive "System 1" versus slow, deliberate "System 2") to a wide audience. He held academic positions at institutions including Hebrew University…

2024-01-death-rivera.r:
Chita Rivera has died. She passed away on January 30, 2024, in New York City, at the age of 91, following a brief illness. Her death came just one week after her 91st birthday (she was born January 23, 1933).

Rivera was one of Broadway's most celebrated performers, with a career spanning more than six decades. Among her most famous achievements:

- Originating the role of **Anita** in *West Side Story* (1957)
- Originating **Velma Kelly** in *Chicago* (1975)
- Starring in *Bye Bye Birdie*, *The Rink*, and *Kiss of the Spider Woman*
- Winning **two competitive Tony Awards** (for *The Rink* and *Kiss of the Spider Woman*), plus a special Tony Award for Lifetime Achievement in 2018
- Receiving…

2024-02-office-mcconnell.r:
On **February 28, 2024**, Mitch McConnell announced on the Senate floor that he would **step down as Senate Republican leader** in November 2024, when the conference was scheduled to hold its leadership elections after the general election.

Key details of his announcement:

- He said it was time for "the next generation of leadership" to take over the conference.
- He made clear he would **not resign from the Senate**—he planned to serve out the remainder of his term, which runs through January 2027.
- At 82 years old, he was the **longest-serving party leader in Senate history**, having led Senate Republicans since 2007, including stints as both majority and minority leader.

2024-03-death-toriyama.r:
Akira Toriyama has died. He passed away on March 1, 2024, at the age of 68. The cause of death was an acute subdural hematoma (a type of bleeding around the brain). His death was announced publicly on March 8, 2024, by his production company, Bird Studio.

Toriyama was born on April 5, 1955, in Aichi Prefecture, Japan. Beyond Dragon Ball, he was also known for creating *Dr. Slump* and for his character design work on the *Dragon Quest* video game series and *Chrono Trigger*. His work had an enormous global influence on manga, anime, and pop culture.

2024-02-office-finland.r:
**Alexander Stubb** won the 2024 Finnish presidential election, succeeding Sauli Niinistö.

Key details:
- The election went to a second round (runoff) on **February 11, 2024**, where Stubb defeated former Foreign Minister Pekka Haavisto with roughly 51.6% of the vote.
- Stubb, a member of the center-right National Coalition Party, previously served as Finland's Prime Minister (2014–2015), as well as Foreign Minister and Finance Minister.
- He was inaugurated as Finland's 13th president on **March 1, 2024**.

Niinistö had served the maximum two consecutive terms (2012–2024) and was therefore ineligible to run again.

2024-03-office-rnc.r: Michael Whatley was elected chair of the Republican National Committee on March 8, 2024, succeeding Ronna McDaniel. Whatley had previously served as chairman of the North Carolina Republican Party and was backed by Donald Trump for the role. At the same meeting, Lara Trump was elected as co-chair of the committee.

2024-03-death-mortensen.r:
Chris Mortensen has died. He passed away on March 3, 2024, at the age of 72.

Mortensen had been diagnosed with Stage IV throat cancer in 2016. He took a leave of absence from ESPN for treatment but returned to work and continued covering the NFL for years afterward. He had been with ESPN for 32 years, joining the network in 1991, and was one of the most prominent NFL insiders in sports media, regularly appearing on Sunday NFL Countdown and breaking major league news. Before ESPN, he worked at the Atlanta Journal-Constitution and The National.

His death was announced by ESPN, and tributes poured in from across the NFL and sports journalism world, with colleagues remembering him as a legenda…

2024-01-office-harvard.r:
No, Claudine Gay is no longer president of Harvard University. She resigned on January 2, 2024, after serving just six months—the shortest presidential tenure in Harvard's history.

Her resignation came amid intense controversy, including criticism of her December 2023 congressional testimony on campus antisemitism and subsequent allegations of plagiarism in her academic work.

Alan Garber, Harvard's provost and chief academic officer (an economist and physician), took over as interim president immediately upon her resignation. In August 2024, the university announced that Garber would serve as Harvard's 31st president on a permanent basis, dropping the interim title. Gay returned to the Har…

2024-02-death-richardlewis.r:
Richard Lewis has died. He passed away on February 27, 2024, at his home in Los Angeles. He was 76 years old, and the cause of death was a heart attack.

Lewis had announced in April 2023 that he had been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease and was retiring from stand-up comedy, though he continued to appear on *Curb Your Enthusiasm* through its final season, which aired in 2024. He played a fictionalized version of himself as one of Larry David's longtime friends on the show, appearing in the series since its debut in 2000.

2024-04-death-betts.r:
Dickey Betts is dead. He died on April 18, 2024, at his home in Osprey, Florida, at the age of 80. According to statements from his family, the causes were cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Betts was a founding member of the Allman Brothers Band and wrote some of their most famous songs, including "Ramblin' Man," "Jessica," and "Blue Sky." He was born on December 12, 1943, in West Palm Beach, Florida.

2024-03-death-walsh.r:
M. Emmet Walsh died on **March 19, 2024**, just three days before his 89th birthday (he was born March 22, 1935). According to reports, he died of cardiac arrest at a hospital in St. Albans, Vermont, near where he lived.

He had a career spanning more than five decades with well over 200 film and television credits. Besides his memorable roles as Captain Bryant in *Blade Runner* (1982) and the scheming private detective Loren Visser in the Coen Brothers' *Blood Simple* (1984), he appeared in films such as *Raising Arizona*, *My Best Friend's Wedding*, *The Jerk*, *Ordinary People*, and *Knives Out* (2019), which was among his final roles. He was widely regarded as one of Hollywood's most rel…

2024-04-death-cavalli.r:
**Roberto Cavalli is dead.** The Italian fashion designer died on **April 12, 2024**, at his home in Florence, Italy. He was 83 years old.

Cavalli, born in Florence in 1940, was famous for his bold animal prints, glamorous designs, and sandblasted denim. He founded his eponymous fashion house in the early 1970s and became a favorite of celebrities for decades. His death was announced by his company in April 2024.

2024-04-death-graham.r:

Terry Anderson is dead. He died on April 21, 2024, at his home in Greenwood Lake, New York. He was 76 years old. According to reports at the time, the cause was complications from recent heart surgery.

He was held for nearly seven years—longer than any other American hostage in Lebanon—before being released on December 4, 1991. After his release, he wrote a memoir, *Den of Lions*, taught journalism, and remained an advocate for hostages and press freedom. His death was announced by his daughter, journalist Sulome Anderson.

Both men had been released from prison only weeks before the vote under an amnesty law.

O.J. Simpson has died. He passed away on **April 10, 2024**, at his home in Las Vegas, Nevada, at the age of 76. The cause of death was prostate cancer, which he had been battling for some time. His family announced his death the following day, stating that he was surrounded by his children and grandchildren when he died.

Simpson was, of course, famously known as a Hall of Fame NFL running back and actor, but became most notorious for his 1995 acquittal in the murders of his ex-wife Nicole Brown Simpson and her friend Ronald Goldman. Peter Higgs is **dead**. He died on **April 8, 2024**, at the age of 94, at his home in Edinburgh, Scotland.

Higgs was born on May 29, 1929, and was best known for proposing the existence of the Higgs boson (and the associated Higgs mechanism) in 1964. After the particle was discovered at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 2013, jointly with François Englert. He spent much of his career at the University of Edinburgh, which announced his death.

2024-05-death-hill.r:
Bernard Hill died on **May 5, 2024**, at the age of 79. His death was announced by his agent, who confirmed he passed away in the early hours of that morning. His fiancée and son were reportedly with him at the time.

Hill was widely known for playing King Théoden in *The Lord of the Rings* trilogy and Captain Edward Smith in *Titanic* (1997), as well as his acclaimed early role as Yosser Hughes in the British drama *Boys from the Blackstuff* (1982). His death coincided with the broadcast of the second series of the BBC drama *The Responder*, in which he had a role.

2024-05-death-colin.r:
Charlie Colin has died. He passed away in May 2024 at the age of 58. According to reports, he died after slipping and falling in the shower while house-sitting for a friend in Brussels, Belgium. His death was confirmed by his mother and reported in the media around May 22, 2024; his body was reportedly found when the friends returned home from their trip.

Colin was a founding member of Train, formed in San Francisco in the mid-1990s, and played bass on their early albums, including their self-titled debut (1998) and the Grammy-winning "Drops of Jupiter" (2001), before departing the band around 2003.

2024-04-office-ireland.r:

2024-08-death-bean.r:
Billy Bean is dead. He died on **August 6, 2024**, at the age of 60, after a battle with acute myeloid leukemia, which he had been diagnosed with in 2023.

Bean played in the majors from 1987 to 1995 (with the Detroit Tigers, Los Angeles Dodgers, and San Diego Padres) and came out publicly as gay in 1999, becoming one of the first former MLB players to do so. In 2014, MLB named him its first-ever Ambassador for Inclusion, and he later served as a senior vice president and special assistant to the commissioner, working on diversity and LGBTQ inclusion initiatives throughout the league.

Note: He should not be confused with Billy Beane (spelled with an "e"), the Oakland Athletics executive of …

2024-08-death-wojcicki.r:
Susan Wojcicki has died. She passed away on **August 9, 2024**, at the age of 56, after living with lung cancer for about two years.

Wojcicki was a prominent tech executive — she served as CEO of YouTube from 2014 to 2023 and was one of Google's earliest employees. Google famously began in her garage in Menlo Park, California, which she rented to founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin in 1998.

Her death came just months after a family tragedy: her 19-year-old son, Marco Troper, died in February 2024. Her husband, Dennis Troper, announced her passing, and she was survived by him and their four other children.

2024-08-death-delon.r:
Alain Delon has died. He passed away on **August 18, 2024**, at the age of 88, at his home in Douchy, in the Loiret region of France. His death was announced by his family.

Delon had been in declining health for several years, having suffered a stroke in 2019, and his son had disclosed in 2023 that he was battling cancer.

He was one of the most iconic figures in French and European cinema, celebrated for roles in films such as *Purple Noon* (1960), *The Leopard* (1963), *Le Samouraï* (1967), and *La Piscine* (1969).

2024-09-death-jones.r:
James Earl Jones died on September 9, 2024, at his home in Dutchess County, New York. He was 93 years old.

He was one of the most acclaimed actors of his generation, known for his distinctive deep voice. His most famous roles included voicing Darth Vader in the Star Wars films and Mufasa in The Lion King, as well as his celebrated stage and screen performances in works like *The Great White Hope* and *Fences*. He was one of the few performers to achieve EGOT status (winning an Emmy, Grammy, Oscar, and Tony), with his Oscar being an honorary award.

2024-08-office-niccol.r:
**Brian Niccol** was named chairman and chief executive officer of Starbucks, replacing Laxman Narasimhan. The announcement was made in August 2024, with Niccol officially taking over on September 9, 2024.

Niccol previously served as CEO of Chipotle Mexican Grill, where he was credited with leading a successful turnaround of the company since 2018. Before Chipotle, he was CEO of Taco Bell. His appointment was well received by investors—Starbucks' stock jumped roughly 24% on the day of the announcement.

Narasimhan, who had taken over as CEO in March 2023 (succeeding longtime leader Howard Schultz), departed after a relatively short tenure marked by declining sales and pressure from activist…

2024-07-death-jones.r:
Jacoby Jones has died. The former NFL wide receiver and return specialist passed away on July 14, 2024, at his home in New Orleans, Louisiana. He was 40 years old, having celebrated his 40th birthday just three days earlier on July 11.

Jones was best known for his time with the Baltimore Ravens, where he played a pivotal role in their Super Bowl XLVII victory over the San Francisco 49ers. In that game, he returned a kickoff 108 yards for a touchdown—one of the most memorable plays in Super Bowl history. He was also on the receiving end of the famous "Mile High Miracle," a 70-yard touchdown catch from Joe Flacco in the closing seconds of a playoff game against Denver.

During his career, he …

2024-08-office-menendez.r:
No, Bob Menendez is no longer a U.S. Senator. He resigned from office on August 20, 2024.

**Why he left office:**

Menendez, a Democrat who had represented New Jersey in the Senate since 2006, was convicted in July 2024 on federal corruption charges following a trial in New York. A jury found him guilty on all 16 counts, including:

- Bribery (accepting gold bars, hundreds of thousands of dollars in cash, and a luxury car)
- Extortion and conspiracy
- Acting as a foreign agent on behalf of the Egyptian government — making him the first sitting member of Congress ever convicted of that offense

Facing near-certain expulsion from the Senate and intense pressure from fellow Democrats, Menendez…

2024-08-office-yunus.r:
**Muhammad Yunus** leads Bangladesh's interim government as its chief adviser.

Key facts:
- Yunus is a Nobel Peace Prize laureate (awarded in 2006) and economist, best known as the founder of Grameen Bank and a pioneer of microcredit.
- He was sworn in as chief adviser on **August 8, 2024**, three days after Sheikh Hasina resigned as prime minister and fled the country amid mass protests.
- His appointment came at the request of the student leaders who had spearheaded the protest movement, and he was formally appointed by President Mohammed Shahabuddin.
- The interim government was tasked with restoring order and preparing the country for new elections.

2024-06-office-india.r:
Assuming you mean the most recent general election (2024): **Narendra Modi** was sworn in as Prime Minister of India for a third consecutive term on June 9, 2024.

However, **no, his party did not win an outright majority on its own**. The BJP won 240 seats in the 543-seat Lok Sabha, falling short of the 272 needed for a majority. This was a notable shift from 2014 (282 seats) and 2019 (303 seats), when the BJP had secured majorities independently. Modi was able to form the government because the broader BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) coalition won 293 seats in total, with key support from allies like the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) and Janata Dal (United).

If you were asking about…

2024-09-death-ashton.r:
John Ashton has died. He passed away on September 26, 2024, at his home in Fort Collins, Colorado, at the age of 76, following a battle with cancer.

His death came just a few months after he reprised his role as John Taggart in *Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F*, which was released on Netflix in July 2024. In that film, his character had risen to become the Beverly Hills police chief. Ashton was also well known for his role in *Midnight Run* (1988) alongside Robert De Niro, in addition to his appearances in the first two *Beverly Hills Cop* films (1984 and 1987).

2024-08-office-sinwar.r:
Yahya Sinwar was chosen to lead Hamas's political bureau after Ismail Haniyeh was killed in Tehran on July 31, 2024. The announcement was made on August 6, 2024. Sinwar had already been leading Hamas in the Gaza Strip and was considered one of the masterminds of the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel.

His tenure was brief—Sinwar himself was killed by Israeli forces in Rafah, Gaza, on October 16, 2024. Following his death, Hamas initially adopted a collective leadership arrangement, with senior figures including Khaled Mashal taking on acting leadership roles.

2024-09-death-rose.r:
Pete Rose has died. He passed away on **September 30, 2024**, at his home in Las Vegas, Nevada, at the age of 83. The cause of death was reported as cardiovascular disease (hypertensive and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease).

Rose remains Major League Baseball's all-time hits leader with 4,256 career hits, earned primarily during his 24-year playing career, most notably with the Cincinnati Reds. He was famously banned from baseball in 1989 for betting on games while managing the Reds, which kept him out of the Hall of Fame during his lifetime.

2024-09-death-jackson.r:
Tito Jackson has died. He passed away on September 15, 2024, at the age of 70.

According to reports at the time, he suffered an apparent heart attack while driving from New Mexico to Oklahoma, and he was pronounced dead at a hospital in Gallup, New Mexico. His death was announced by his three sons—Taj, Taryll, and TJ Jackson, who perform together as the group 3T—in a statement posted on social media.

Tito, born Toriano Adaryll Jackson on October 15, 1953, was the third-eldest of the Jackson siblings. He played guitar and sang in the Jackson 5 and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with the group in 1997. At the time of his death, he was still performing alongside his brothers…

2024-08-office-paetongtarn.r:
Following the Constitutional Court's removal of Srettha Thavisin on August 14, 2024, **Paetongtarn Shinawatra** was elected Prime Minister by parliament on August 16, 2024. The leader of the Pheu Thai Party and daughter of former Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra, she became Thailand's youngest-ever prime minister at age 37.

It's worth noting that her tenure also ended in court action: the Constitutional Court suspended her in July 2025 over a leaked phone call with Cambodian leader Hun Sen, and removed her from office on August 29, 2025. Parliament then elected **Anutin Charnvirakul** of the Bhumjaithai Party as prime minister in September 2025.

2024-09-office-hill.r:
**Elliott Hill** was named to become President and Chief Executive Officer of Nike, Inc., replacing John Donahoe. The announcement was made in September 2024, with Hill taking over the role effective October 14, 2024.

Hill is a longtime Nike veteran who spent more than 30 years at the company, starting as an intern in 1988 and eventually rising to President of Consumer and Marketplace before retiring in 2020. He came out of retirement to take the CEO position.

Donahoe, a former eBay and ServiceNow executive who had led Nike since January 2020, stepped down amid the company's struggles with declining sales, a faltering stock price, and increased competition from newer athletic brands.

2024-09-death-smith.r:
Dame Maggie Smith died on September 27, 2024, at the age of 89. She passed away peacefully in a London hospital, according to a statement released by her sons, actors Toby Stephens and Chris Larkin.

Born on December 28, 1934, she had a career spanning more than seven decades. She won two Academy Awards—for *The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie* (1969) and *California Suite* (1978)—and became widely known to newer generations as Professor Minerva McGonagall in the *Harry Potter* films and as the Dowager Countess Violet Crawley in *Downton Abbey*. She was made a Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire in 1990.

2024-09-death-kristofferson.r:
Kris Kristofferson died on September 28, 2024, at the age of 88. He passed away peacefully at his home in Maui, Hawaii, according to a statement from his family.

Kristofferson was a legendary figure in country music, known for writing classics like "Me and Bobby McGee," "Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down," and "Help Me Make It Through the Night." He was also a member of the supergroup The Highwaymen alongside Johnny Cash, Waylon Jennings, and Willie Nelson. As an actor, he starred in films such as "A Star Is Born" (1976), for which he won a Golden Globe, and played Whistler in the "Blade" film series. He had retired from performing in 2021.

2024-10-death-gaynor.r:
Mitzi Gaynor died on October 17, 2024, at the age of 93. She passed away in Los Angeles of natural causes, as confirmed by her longtime management team.

Born on September 4, 1931, in Chicago, Gaynor was best known for her starring role as Ensign Nellie Forbush in the 1958 film adaptation of Rodgers and Hammerstein's *South Pacific*. Her other notable film credits included *There's No Business Like Show Business* (1954), *Anything Goes* (1956), and *Les Girls* (1957). She later became a popular television variety show star and a successful Las Vegas performer. At the time of her death, she was one of the last surviving stars of Hollywood's Golden Age musical era.

2024-08-office-hasina.r:
No, Sheikh Hasina is no longer the Prime Minister of Bangladesh.

**What happened:** She resigned on August 5, 2024, and fled to India aboard a military aircraft as protesters stormed her official residence in Dhaka. This ended her 15-year consecutive tenure as prime minister (over 20 years total, counting her earlier term from 1996–2001).

**Background:** Her downfall followed weeks of massive student-led protests that began over a controversial quota system for government jobs. The demonstrations escalated into a nationwide anti-government movement after security forces responded with a violent crackdown that killed hundreds of people. When the army declined to continue suppressing the pro…

2024-09-death-nasrallah.r:
**Hassan Nasrallah is dead.** He was killed on **September 27, 2024**, in an Israeli airstrike on Hezbollah's central headquarters in the Dahieh district of southern Beirut, Lebanon.

Key details:

- **How he died:** Israel dropped dozens of bunker-buster bombs on the underground complex where Nasrallah was meeting with senior Hezbollah commanders. The strike destroyed multiple buildings and also killed other top figures, including Ali Karaki, commander of Hezbollah's Southern Front, and a senior Iranian Revolutionary Guard commander.
- **Confirmation:** The Israeli military announced his death on September 28, and Hezbollah subsequently confirmed it. He was 64 years old and had led Hezbolla…

2024-10-death-garr.r:
Teri Garr has died. She passed away on October 29, 2024, in Los Angeles at the age of 79. Her death was attributed to complications from multiple sclerosis, a condition she had lived with for decades—she publicly disclosed her MS diagnosis in 2002 and later became an advocate for MS awareness and research.

Garr had a prolific career spanning several decades. She earned an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actress for her role as Sandy Lester in *Tootsie* (1982), and she was beloved for her comedic performances in films like *Young Frankenstein* (1974), where she played Inga, as well as *Close Encounters of the Third Kind* (1977) and *Mr. Mom* (1983). She largely retired from acti…

2024-09-office-barnier.r:
Emmanuel Macron appointed **Michel Barnier** as Prime Minister of France on September 5, 2024, succeeding Gabriel Attal. Barnier, a veteran conservative from Les Républicains and the EU's former chief Brexit negotiator, took office after the snap legislative elections of June–July 2024 produced a hung parliament.

It's worth noting that Barnier's tenure was short-lived: his government was toppled by a no-confidence vote in December 2024—the first successful such vote in France since 1962. Macron then appointed **François Bayrou**, the centrist MoDem leader, as Prime Minister.

2024-10-death-lesh.r:
Phil Lesh died on **October 25, 2024**, at the age of 84. His death was announced on his official social media accounts, which stated that he passed away peacefully, surrounded by family. No specific cause of death was disclosed in the initial announcement, though he had faced various health challenges over the years, including hepatitis C (which led to a liver transplant in 1998) and a bout with bladder cancer.

Lesh co-founded the Grateful Dead in 1965 (originally as the Warlocks) in Palo Alto, California, and was known for his innovative, contrapuntal approach to bass playing, influenced by his background in classical and avant-garde music. He remained musically active for decades after t…

2024-10-death-salmond.r:
Alex Salmond died on **October 12, 2024**. He collapsed and died suddenly after giving a speech at a conference in Ohrid, North Macedonia. The reported cause of death was a heart attack. He was 69 years old (born December 31, 1954).

At the time of his death, he was the leader of the Alba Party, which he founded in 2021 after leaving the SNP. Tributes were paid from across the political spectrum, including from figures he had fallen out with in recent years, such as his former deputy Nicola Sturgeon.

2024-10-death-payne.r:
Liam Payne has died. He passed away on **October 16, 2024**, at the age of 31.

**How he died:** Payne fell from a third-floor balcony at the CasaSur Palermo Hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina, where he had been staying. The cause of death was determined to be multiple traumatic injuries ("polytrauma") from the fall.

**Additional context:**
- Prior to the fall, hotel staff had called emergency services reporting a guest behaving erratically, possibly under the influence of drugs and alcohol.
- A toxicology report found alcohol, cocaine, and a prescription antidepressant in his system at the time of death.
- Argentine prosecutors investigated the circumstances, and several people — including h…

2024-09-office-dissanayake.r:
**Anura Kumara Dissanayake** won Sri Lanka's presidential election held on September 21, 2024. He is the leader of the left-wing Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP) and ran under the National People's Power (NPP) alliance.

Key details:
- The incumbent, **Ranil Wickremesinghe** (who had become president in 2022 after Gotabaya Rajapaksa resigned amid mass protests over the economic crisis), ran as an independent but finished third and was eliminated in the first round of counting.
- Under Sri Lanka's preferential voting system, no candidate won over 50% of first-preference votes, so a second count was held. Dissanayake defeated Sajith Premadasa of the Samagi Jana Balawegaya (SJB) with roughly 42%…

2024-10-death-tata.r:
Ratan Tata has died. He passed away on **October 9, 2024**, in Mumbai, India, at the age of 86. He had been hospitalized at Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai in the days leading up to his death. His death was confirmed by Tata Sons, and he was given a state funeral in Mumbai on October 10, 2024, which was attended by prominent political and business figures.

Ratan Tata served as chairman of Tata Sons from 1991 to 2012 (and briefly as interim chairman in 2016–2017) and is widely regarded as one of India's most respected business leaders, credited with transforming the Tata Group into a global conglomerate.

2024-10-death-valenzuela.r:
Fernando Valenzuela has died. He passed away on **October 22, 2024**, at the age of 63, in Los Angeles.

His death came just days before the start of the 2024 World Series between the Dodgers and the New York Yankees. The Dodgers honored him throughout the series, including wearing a patch with his number 34, and went on to win the championship.

Valenzuela was one of the most beloved figures in Dodgers history. A left-handed pitcher from Mexico, he sparked "Fernandomania" in 1981, when he won both the National League Cy Young Award and Rookie of the Year while helping lead the Dodgers to a World Series title. The Dodgers retired his number 34 in 2023. He had also served as a Spanish-languag…

2024-09-office-ishiba.r:
**Sanae Takaichi** won the most recent Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) leadership election on October 4, 2025, defeating Shinjiro Koizumi in a runoff vote. She subsequently became Japan's first female prime minister on October 21, 2025.

Some context:
- The election was triggered by Shigeru Ishiba's resignation in September 2025, following the LDP's poor results in both the October 2024 lower house election and the July 2025 upper house election, which left the ruling coalition without a majority in either chamber.
- Takaichi, a conservative known for her hawkish views on defense and her admiration for former PM Shinzo Abe, had previously run for the leadership in 2024, when she lost to Ishib…

2024-10-office-ishiba.r:
**Shigeru Ishiba** was elected Prime Minister of Japan, succeeding Fumio Kishida.

Kishida announced in August 2024 that he would not seek re-election as leader of the ruling Liberal Democratic Party (LDP), amid low approval ratings and a party slush fund scandal. Ishiba, a former Defense Minister and longtime LDP figure, won the party's leadership election on September 27, 2024, defeating Economic Security Minister Sanae Takaichi in a runoff vote. He was formally elected Prime Minister by the National Diet on October 1, 2024.

Ishiba subsequently called a snap general election for October 27, 2024, in which the LDP-Komeito coalition lost its lower house majority. Nevertheless, he was re-ele…

2024-10-office-nike.r:
**Elliott Hill** is the president and chief executive officer of Nike, having succeeded John Donahoe in October 2024.

Hill is a longtime Nike veteran who spent more than 30 years at the company before retiring in 2020. During his earlier tenure, he held several senior leadership roles, including President of Consumer and Marketplace, where he oversaw Nike's commercial and marketing operations. He came out of retirement to take the top job as part of Nike's effort to revitalize the brand amid slowing sales and increased competition.

John Donahoe, who had served as CEO since January 2020 (following Mark Parker), stepped down in October 2024 after a tenure marked by a push toward direct-to-co…

2024-11-death-bradford.r:
Barbara Taylor Bradford has died. She passed away on **November 24, 2024**, at her home in New York City, at the age of 91.

Born in Leeds, England, in 1933, she became one of the world's best-selling authors after her debut novel, *A Woman of Substance* (1979), became an international phenomenon. The book sold tens of millions of copies, was adapted into a popular television miniseries, and launched a long-running saga about the Emma Harte character. Over her career, she wrote more than 40 novels, with total sales estimated in the tens of millions of copies worldwide.

2024-11-death-quincy-jones.r:
Quincy Jones has died. He passed away on November 3, 2024, at his home in the Bel Air neighborhood of Los Angeles, California. He was 91 years old. His death was confirmed by his family and publicist, and the cause was reported to be pancreatic cancer.

Jones was one of the most influential figures in American music, best known for producing Michael Jackson's landmark albums *Off the Wall*, *Thriller*, and *Bad*, as well as for his work with Frank Sinatra, Ray Charles, and many others. Over his career, he won 28 Grammy Awards and was nominated for 80.

2024-10-death-sinwar.r:
Yahya Sinwar is dead. He was killed by Israeli forces on **October 16, 2024**, in Rafah, in the southern Gaza Strip.

Key details of how he was killed:

- **Not a targeted operation**: Interestingly, his death was somewhat incidental. Israeli troops from the 828th Brigade encountered a small group of militants during a routine operation in the Tal al-Sultan neighborhood of Rafah — they did not initially know Sinwar was among them.
- **The firefight**: After an exchange of fire, the militants took cover in a damaged building. An Israeli tank fired on the building, and a drone was sent in to survey the damage.
- **Drone footage**: Footage later released by the IDF showed a wounded man — later …

2024-11-death-balaji.r:
Suchir Balaji has died. He was found dead in his San Francisco apartment on **November 26, 2024**, at the age of 26.

Balaji was a former OpenAI researcher who had publicly criticized the company, notably in an October 2024 New York Times interview where he argued that OpenAI's practice of training its models on copyrighted material violated "fair use" doctrine and harmed the internet ecosystem.

**Regarding the circumstances of his death:**
- The San Francisco Medical Examiner's Office ruled his death a **suicide** (by gunshot wound). The autopsy report was publicly released in February 2025 confirming this determination.
- However, his parents have publicly disputed the suicide ruling, rai…

2024-11-death-jamison.r:
Judith Jamison died on November 9, 2024, at the age of 81. She died in New York City, reportedly after a brief illness.

Jamison was one of the most celebrated figures in modern dance. She joined the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater in 1965 and became famous for her performances, most notably in "Cry," the iconic solo Alvin Ailey choreographed for her in 1971. After leaving the company in 1980 to pursue other projects, she returned in 1989 to become artistic director following Ailey's death, leading the company for more than two decades until her retirement in 2011. She was succeeded by Robert Battle.

2024-10-office-japan-election.r:
They **lost** it. In the most recent House of Representatives general election I know of — held **27 October 2024** — the LDP won 191 seats and Komeito 24, for a coalition total of **215 seats**, below the **233** needed for a majority in the 465-seat chamber. It was the first time since 2009 that the LDP-led coalition fell short of a lower-house majority, leaving Prime Minister Shigeru Ishiba heading a minority government.

If a snap lower-house election has occurred since my information cutoff, I may not have its result.

2024-11-office-hegseth.r:
President-elect Donald Trump has made this nomination twice, during his two presidential transitions:

- **November 2024**: Trump nominated **Pete Hegseth**, a Fox News host and Army National Guard veteran, to serve as Secretary of Defense for his second term. Hegseth was confirmed by the Senate on January 24, 2025, in a 51–50 vote, with Vice President JD Vance casting the tie-breaking vote.

- **December 2016**: During his first transition, Trump nominated retired Marine Corps General **James Mattis**, who was confirmed in January 2017 and served until early 2019.

If you're asking about the most recent nomination (the 2024 transition), the answer is Pete Hegseth.

2024-12-death-carter.r:
Former President Jimmy Carter died on December 29, 2024, at his home in Plains, Georgia. He was 100 years old, making him the longest-lived president in U.S. history.

Carter had entered hospice care in February 2023, choosing to spend his remaining time at home rather than pursue additional medical intervention. His wife of 77 years, Rosalynn Carter, died in November 2023, and he attended her memorial service shortly before his own death.

Carter served as the 39th president from 1977 to 1981. After leaving office, he became widely admired for his humanitarian work, including his efforts with Habitat for Humanity and the Carter Center, which earned him the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002.

2024-11-office-trump-election.r:
The most recent U.S. presidential election was held on November 5, 2024. **Donald Trump** won, defeating **Kamala Harris**, the Democratic nominee and sitting Vice President.

Key details:
- Trump won 312 electoral votes to Harris's 226
- He also won the popular vote, receiving roughly 49.8% compared to Harris's roughly 48.3%
- Trump was inaugurated on January 20, 2025, becoming the 47th president
- He is the second president in U.S. history to serve non-consecutive terms (after Grover Cleveland), having previously served as the 45th president from 2017 to 2021

2024-11-office-mauritius.r: Following Mauritius’s general election on 10 November 2024, **Navin Ramgoolam** became prime minister. His opposition **Alliance du Changement** (led by his Labour Party) won a landslide, and he replaced **Pravind Jugnauth**, the incumbent MSM leader who had been prime minister since 2017. It was a return to the office for Ramgoolam, who had previously served as prime minister from 2005 to 2014.

2024-11-death-west.r:
Timothy West, the British actor, has died. He passed away on **November 12, 2024**, at the age of 90. According to a statement released by his family, he died peacefully in his sleep, with his family around him.

Born on October 20, 1934, in Bradford, England, West had a distinguished career spanning more than six decades on stage and screen. He was particularly well known for:

- Playing the title role in the TV series **"Edward the Seventh"** (1975)
- The sitcom **"Brass"** (1983–1990)
- Numerous Shakespearean and classical stage roles
- The documentary series **"Great Canal Journeys"** (2014–2021), which he presented alongside his wife, actress Prunella Scales

He was married to Prunella …

2024-12-death-singh.r:
Former Indian Prime Minister Manmohan Singh has died. He passed away on **December 26, 2024**, at the age of 92.

He was admitted to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in New Delhi that evening after his health deteriorated, and he died later that night. He had been in declining health for some time and had retired from the Rajya Sabha (the upper house of India's Parliament) in April 2024.

Singh served as Prime Minister from 2004 to 2014, leading the Congress party–led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government. Before that, he was widely credited as the architect of India's 1991 economic liberalization reforms during his tenure as Finance Minister. Following his death, t…

2024-12-death-gumbel.r:
Greg Gumbel has died. He passed away on December 27, 2024, at the age of 78. According to a statement released by his family through CBS Sports, he died peacefully, surrounded by loved ones, after a battle with cancer.

Gumbel was a pioneering sportscaster best known for his long career at CBS Sports, where he hosted "The NFL Today" and served as a play-by-play announcer for NFL games and NCAA basketball. In 2001, he became the first African-American announcer to call play-by-play for a major U.S. sports championship when he called Super Bowl XXXV. Earlier in 2024, he had notably missed covering the NCAA men's basketball tournament—his first absence from March Madness coverage in decades—due…

2024-11-office-gaetz.r:
President-elect Donald Trump first nominated former U.S. Representative Matt Gaetz of Florida to be Attorney General, announcing the pick on November 13, 2024. No, Gaetz did not go on to hold the office. He withdrew from consideration on November 21, 2024, amid controversy over a House Ethics Committee investigation and allegations of sexual misconduct, saying his confirmation had become a distraction. Trump then nominated former Florida Attorney General Pam Bondi, who was confirmed by the Senate and sworn in as Attorney General in February 2025.

(If you were asking about Trump's first term instead: after the 2016 election, he nominated Senator Jeff Sessions of Alabama, who was confirmed an…

2024-12-death-giovanni.r:
Nikki Giovanni has died. She passed away on **December 9, 2024**, at the age of 81, in Blacksburg, Virginia. Her death was due to complications from lung cancer, a disease she had battled for many years.

Giovanni was born on June 7, 1943, in Knoxville, Tennessee, and rose to prominence in the late 1960s as a leading voice of the Black Arts Movement. Her acclaimed works include *Black Feeling, Black Talk* (1968), *Black Judgement* (1968), and the widely celebrated poem "Ego Tripping (there may be a reason why)." She was also a longtime professor at Virginia Tech, where she taught for over three decades, and she gained national attention for her poem "We Are Virginia Tech," delivered after th…

2024-12-office-mahama.r:
**John Dramani Mahama** won Ghana's most recent presidential election, held on December 7, 2024.

Key details:
- Mahama, of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), defeated Mahamudu Bawumia, the sitting Vice President and candidate of the New Patriotic Party (NPP)
- Mahama won with roughly 56–57% of the vote; Bawumia conceded defeat on December 8, 2024
- This marked a historic comeback—Mahama previously served as president from 2012 to 2017, lost re-election in 2016, and lost again in 2020 before winning in 2024
- He was sworn in on January 7, 2025
- His running mate, Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang, became Ghana's first female Vice President

The NDC also won a strong majority in parliament. The …

2024-12-death-thompson.r:
Brian Thompson has died. He was shot and killed on December 4, 2024, in New York City.

**What happened:**
- Thompson, 50, was shot outside the New York Hilton Midtown hotel in Manhattan early that morning (around 6:45 a.m.), where he was heading to speak at UnitedHealth Group's annual investor conference.
- The shooting appeared to be a targeted attack. The masked gunman approached from behind, fired multiple shots, and fled the scene, eventually escaping into Central Park on an e-bike.

**The investigation and arrest:**
- After a days-long manhunt, Luigi Mangione was arrested on December 9, 2024, at a McDonald's in Altoona, Pennsylvania. He was charged with the murder.
- Mangione was repor…

2024-11-office-lindner.r:

2026-06-office-colombia.r:
**Gustavo Petro** won Colombia's most recent presidential election. He defeated Rodolfo Hernández in a runoff on **June 19, 2022**, winning about 50.4% of the vote, and took office on **August 7, 2022**.

A few notable facts about his victory:
- He became Colombia's **first left-wing president**
- His running mate, **Francia Márquez**, became the country's first Afro-Colombian vice president
- He ran as the candidate of the left-wing Pacto Histórico coalition

Colombian presidents serve four-year terms and cannot be consecutively re-elected, so the next presidential election is scheduled for 2026. As of my knowledge cutoff (early 2025), Petro remains in office.

2024-02-death-kiptum.r:
Kelvin Kiptum is dead.

The Kenyan marathon world record holder died on 11 February 2024 at age 24 in a road traffic accident near Kaptagat, Elgeyo-Marakwet County, Kenya.

He was killed alongside his coach, Gervais Hakizimana, when the car they were in veered off the road on the Eldoret-Kaptagat highway. Kiptum had set the marathon world record of 2:00:35 at the Chicago Marathon in October 2023.

2024-02-death-brehme.r:
Andreas Brehme died.

The former West Germany / Germany left-back and 1990 World Cup winner passed away on 20 February 2024 in Munich, Germany, at the age of 63. The death was announced publicly on 22 February 2024. He was reported to have died of a heart attack.

2024-01-death-musser.r:
Alec Musser is deceased.

The actor who played Ryan Lavery on *All My Children* and had a small role in Adam Sandler’s *Grown Ups* was found dead in his Palm Springs, California apartment in early January 2024. He was 50 years old.

He was found on 6 January 2024 and the death was publicly reported on 7 January 2024. Palm Springs police said there was no sign of foul play and the cause of death was under investigation at the time of the report.

2024-01-office-harvard.r:
No. Claudine Gay is no longer President of Harvard.

She resigned effective January 2, 2024, about six months after taking office in July 2023. The resignation came after intense criticism over her congressional testimony on antisemitism on campus and subsequent plagiarism allegations.

Alan M. Garber, Harvard's Provost and former dean of Harvard Medical School, succeeded her immediately as Interim President on January 2, 2024.

2024-01-office-guatemala.r:
The president who took office after the 2023 general election is **Bernardo Arévalo de León of the Semilla party**.

Arévalo was declared the winner of the 20 August 2023 second round and was certified by the Supreme Electoral Tribunal, TSE, in December 2023. His inauguration was set for 14 January 2024 under the Constitution.

The handover was made contentious by months of legal and political obstruction by the Attorney General’s Office and allies of the outgoing government, who sought to annul Semilla’s registration and block Arévalo’s assumption of power. After a standoff in the National Congress on the morning of 14 January, Arévalo was sworn in as the 51st President of Guatemala and Kar…

2024-02-death-navalny.r:
Alexei Navalny is dead.

He died in custody on 16 February 2024 at age 47. The Federal Penitentiary Service of Russia announced his death that day, saying he lost consciousness after a walk at Penal Colony IK-3 in Kharp, Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Okrug, and could not be revived.

2024-02-death-tobykeith.r:
Country music singer Toby Keith is dead.

He died on May 5, 2024 at age 62 at his home in Oklahoma. His family announced the death the same day, saying he had been privately battling stomach cancer since being diagnosed in 2022.

2024-03-death-carmen.r:
Eric Carmen died.

The singer-songwriter best known for "All By Myself" and "Never Gonna Fall in Love Again" with The Raspberries died on March 11, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio, at age 74.

2024-01-death-zagallo.r:

2024-01-office-bhutan.r:
The National Assembly that was elected in the January 2024 general election, the first round of which was held on 9 January 2024 and the second round on 15 January 2024, returned the Bhutan Tendrel Party, BTP, to power.

The BTP won 31 of the 47 seats in the National Assembly and its leader, Dasho Tshering Tobgay, was sworn in as Prime Minister for a second, non-consecutive term on 28 January 2024. He succeeded Lotay Tshering of the Druk Nyamrup Tshogpa who had been Prime Minister since 2018.

2024-03-death-lieberman.r:
Former U.S. Senator Joe Lieberman of Connecticut is dead.

He died on March 27, 2024 at age 82.

2024-03-death-gossett.r:
Louis Gossett Jr. has died.

He died on March 29, 2024 at age 87 in Santa Monica, California. He was the first Black actor to win the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for *An Officer and a Gentleman* in 1982.

2024-01-office-tko-mcmahon.r:
No. Vince McMahon is no longer Executive Chairman of TKO Group Holdings, the parent company of WWE and UFC, and he is no longer on the TKO board.

He was Executive Chairman of TKO when the company was formed from the WWE-UFC merger in September 2023.

He stepped down from the role on January 23, 2024, and announced an indefinite leave of absence from WWE and TKO. The move came days after The Wall Street Journal reported new allegations that McMahon had engaged in sexual misconduct and had paid hush money to several women, including a former WWE paralegal. A civil lawsuit alleging sexual trafficking and sexual assault by former WWE employee Janel Grant was filed around the same time.

McMahon…
