2024-01-death-zagallo.r:
Mário Zagallo has died. He passed away on **January 5, 2024**, at the age of 92, in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. His death was announced by the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF).

Zagallo was one of the most iconic figures in Brazilian football history. He was the first person to win the FIFA World Cup both as a player and as a head coach:

- **1958** – Won as a player (left winger)
- **1962** – Won as a player
- **1970** – Won as head coach of the legendary Brazil team featuring Pelé
- **1994** – Won as assistant coach, giving him four World Cup titles in total

He is widely remembered as a symbol of Brazilian football's golden era.

2024-01-death-musser.r:
Alec Musser has died. He passed away on **January 13, 2024**, at the age of 50. He was found dead at his home in Del Mar, California. The San Diego County Medical Examiner's office later ruled his death a suicide.

Musser was best known for playing Del Henry on the soap opera *All My Children*, a role he won through the SOAPnet reality competition series *I Wanna Be a Soap Star* in 2005. He also appeared in the 2010 comedy film *Grown Ups* as the water park lifeguard, and worked as a fitness model.

2024-01-death-oliver.r:
Christian Oliver has died. He passed away on **January 4, 2024**, at the age of 51, in a plane crash in the Caribbean.

**Details of the crash:**
- Oliver (born Christian Klepser) was traveling with his two young daughters, **Madita (10) and Annik (12)**, on a small single-engine aircraft departing from Bequia in St. Vincent and the Grenadines.
- The plane, bound for nearby St. Lucia, crashed into the sea shortly after takeoff.
- All four people aboard were killed: Oliver, his two daughters, and the pilot, Robert Sachs.
- Local fishermen and rescue teams recovered the bodies from the water near the crash site.

Oliver was a German-born actor best known for roles in *Speed Racer* (2008), *Sav…

2024-01-office-bhutan.r: After Bhutan's most recent parliamentary elections, held in January 2024, **Tshering Tobgay** of the People's Democratic Party (PDP) took office as prime minister. His party won a decisive victory in the runoff round of voting on January 9, 2024, defeating the Bhutan Tendrel Party led by Pema Chewang. Tobgay was sworn in as prime minister in early February 2024. Notably, this was his second stint in the role, as he had previously served as prime minister from 2013 to 2018.

2024-01-death-beckenbauer.r:
Franz Beckenbauer has died. The German football legend, known as "Der Kaiser," passed away on **January 7, 2024**, at the age of 78. His death was announced by his family the following day. He died at his home in Salzburg, Austria, and the family did not publicly disclose the exact cause of death, though he had experienced significant health problems in his later years, including heart issues.

Beckenbauer is widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of all time. He won the FIFA World Cup as captain of West Germany in 1974 and again as the team's manager in 1990, making him one of only a few people to win the tournament as both a player and a coach. He also won the Ballon d'Or twice…

2024-01-office-drcongo.r: Félix Tshisekedi was sworn in for a new term as president of the Democratic Republic of the Congo following the presidential election held on December 20, 2023. He won re-election decisively, receiving roughly 73% of the vote according to official results announced by the electoral commission (CENI), defeating his main rivals including Moïse Katumbi and Martin Fayulu. He took the oath of office for his second five-year term on January 20, 2024, in a ceremony held in Kinshasa.

2024-01-death-rivera.r:
Chita Rivera has died. The legendary Broadway dancer and actress passed away on **January 30, 2024**, at the age of 91, in New York City, following a brief illness. Her death was announced by her daughter, Lisa Mordente.

Rivera was one of Broadway's most celebrated performers, best known for originating iconic roles such as Anita in *West Side Story* (1957), Velma Kelly in *Chicago* (1975), and Aurora in *Kiss of the Spider Woman* (1993). Over her decades-long career, she earned ten Tony Award nominations, winning three times, and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2009 — the first Hispanic woman to receive that honor.

2024-02-death-brehme.r:
Andreas Brehme has died. He passed away on **February 20, 2024**, at the age of 63. According to reports, he suffered a cardiac arrest and died in a hospital in Munich.

Brehme is best remembered for scoring the winning penalty in the 1990 FIFA World Cup final in Rome, where West Germany defeated Argentina 1-0. He was also known for his time at clubs like Bayern Munich, Inter Milan (where he won the Serie A title in 1989), and 1. FC Kaiserslautern, with whom he won the Bundesliga in 1998.

2024-01-death-soul.r:
David Soul has died. He passed away on **January 4, 2024**, at the age of 80, in London, England, where he had lived for many years (he was a British citizen as well as American). His death was announced by his wife, Helen Snell, who said he died after "a valiant battle for life in the loving company of family." He had reportedly suffered from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) for some time and had been awaiting a lung transplant.

Soul was best known for his role as Detective Kenneth "Hutch" Hutchinson in *Starsky & Hutch* (1975–1979), alongside Paul Michael Glaser. Beyond acting, he was also a successful singer, scoring major hits with "Don't Give Up on Us" (1976) and "Silver La…

2024-02-death-kiptum.r:
Kelvin Kiptum has died. He was killed in a road traffic accident on **February 11, 2024**, in Kenya. He was 24 years old.

Details of the accident:
- The crash occurred on the Eldoret–Kaptagat road in Elgeyo Marakwet County, western Kenya, an area where many Kenyan distance runners train.
- Kiptum was driving when the vehicle he was in veered off the road and struck a tree.
- His coach, **Gervais Hakizimana** of Rwanda, also died in the crash. A third occupant, a woman, was injured.

Kiptum had set the men's marathon world record of **2:00:35** at the Chicago Marathon in October 2023, breaking Eliud Kipchoge's previous mark. At the time of his death, he was preparing to attempt to break the …

2024-01-office-guatemala.r:
**Bernardo Arévalo** is the president of Guatemala who took office after a contentious, delayed inauguration.

Arévalo, a member of the progressive Movimiento Semilla (Seed Movement) party, won the August 2023 presidential election in a runoff against establishment candidate Sandra Torres. However, his path to power was fraught with obstacles:

- Guatemalan prosecutors, led by Attorney General María Consuelo Porras, sought to annul the election results, alleging irregularities in his party's registration.
- The electoral tribunal initially suspended his party, and there were multiple legal challenges aimed at blocking him from taking office.
- On January 14, 2024—the scheduled inauguration d…

2024-01-office-tko-mcmahon.r:
No, Vince McMahon no longer holds the Executive Chairman role at TKO Group Holdings. He resigned from that position, as well as from TKO's board of directors, on **January 26, 2024**.

**Why he left:**

His resignation came just two days after former WWE employee Janel Grant filed a lawsuit against him on January 24, 2024, alleging sexual assault, emotional abuse, and sex trafficking, and claiming that McMahon had paid her millions of dollars to keep silent. The lawsuit also named WWE and former head of talent relations John Laurinaitis as defendants.

In his resignation statement, McMahon maintained his innocence, saying the lawsuit was "replete with lies" and that he intended to vigorously…

2024-02-death-chao.r:
Angela Chao has died. She passed away on **February 10, 2024**, at the age of 50.

**How she died:** Chao drowned after her Tesla Model X reversed into a pond on her ranch near Johnson City in Blanco County, Texas. The vehicle became submerged, and despite efforts by emergency responders to reach her, she did not survive. An investigation later revealed that her blood alcohol content was approximately 0.233% — nearly three times the legal driving limit — indicating that intoxication was likely a factor in the accident.

**Background:** Angela Chao was the youngest of six daughters of shipping magnate James S.C. Chao and took over as chair and CEO of Foremost Group, a New York-based internati…

2024-02-death-weathers.r:
Carl Weathers has died. He passed away on **February 1, 2024**, at the age of 76. His death was announced by his family on February 2, 2024, and it was reported that he died peacefully in his sleep at his home in Los Angeles. The cause of death was attributed to atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

Weathers was best known for portraying Apollo Creed in the first four *Rocky* films, but he also had a long career that included roles in *Predator* (1987), *Happy Gilmore* (1996), and more recently Greef Karga in *The Mandalorian*, for which he also directed episodes and received an Emmy nomination.

2024-02-office-finland.r:
**Alexander Stubb** won the most recent Finnish presidential election, held in early 2024. He defeated Pekka Haavisto in the runoff round on February 11, 2024, receiving roughly 51.6% of the vote.

Stubb, a member of the National Coalition Party (Kokoomus) and a former Prime Minister of Finland, was inaugurated as president on March 1, 2024, succeeding Sauli Niinistö, who had served two six-year terms since 2012 and was ineligible to run again due to term limits.

2024-02-death-richardlewis.r:
Richard Lewis has died. He passed away on **February 27, 2024**, at his home in Los Angeles at the age of 76. According to his publicist, he died of a heart attack.

Some context: Lewis had faced significant health problems in his later years. In April 2023, he publicly revealed that he had been diagnosed with Parkinson's disease about two years earlier, and he retired from stand-up comedy around that time. He also underwent several surgeries in the years prior.

Notably, he had already filmed material for the twelfth and final season of *Curb Your Enthusiasm* before his death, so he appears posthumously in that season, which aired beginning in early 2024.

2024-02-death-tobykeith.r:
Country music singer **Toby Keith has died**. He passed away on **February 5, 2024**, at the age of 62.

Keith had been battling stomach cancer, which he was diagnosed with in the fall of 2021 (he publicly announced his diagnosis in June 2022). He underwent treatment for the disease during that period, even performing some concerts along the way, but ultimately succumbed to it. His death was announced via a statement on his official social media accounts, noting that he died peacefully, surrounded by his family.

Known for hits like "Should've Been a Cowboy," "Courtesy of the Red, White and Blue (The Angry American)," and "Red Solo Cup," Keith was one of country music's most commercially suc…

2024-01-office-harvard.r:
No, Claudine Gay is no longer president of Harvard University. She resigned effective January 8, 2024, after roughly six months in office—the shortest tenure of any Harvard president. She had taken office on July 1, 2023, becoming Harvard's 30th president and the first Black person to hold the role.

Her resignation followed intense controversy stemming from two main issues:
1. **December 2023 congressional testimony**: Her responses at a House hearing on campus antisemitism—where she declined to say definitively that calls for the genocide of Jews would violate Harvard's conduct policies—drew bipartisan criticism.
2. **Plagiarism allegations**: Accusations surfaced regarding inadequate cita…

2024-02-death-navalny.r:
**Alexei Navalny has died.** He passed away on **February 16, 2024**, at the age of 47.

Key details:

- **Where:** He died at the IK-3 penal colony ("Polar Wolf") in Kharp, a remote Arctic settlement in the Yamalo-Nenets Autonomous Region of Siberia, where he had been transferred in December 2023.
- **Official account:** Russian prison authorities said he felt unwell after a walk, lost consciousness, and could not be resuscitated despite emergency efforts.
- **Cause of death:** Russian officials did not publicly release the findings of their medical examination. His family and supporters, along with Western governments, widely blamed President Vladimir Putin and the Russian state, viewing h…

2024-02-office-mcconnell.r:
On **February 28, 2024**, Mitch McConnell announced that he would step down from his position as Senate Republican leader in **November 2024**. 

Key details of the announcement:
- He had served as the top Senate Republican since 2007, making him the longest-serving party leader in Senate history.
- He stated he would remain a U.S. Senator and serve out his current term, which runs through January 2027.
- In November 2024, Senate Republicans elected **John Thune** of South Dakota to succeed him as their leader when the new Congress convened in January 2025.

2024-02-office-indonesia.r:
**Prabowo Subianto** won Indonesia's most recent presidential election, held on **February 14, 2024**.

Key details:
- Prabowo won roughly **58–59% of the vote**, securing a first-round victory over his two rivals, **Anies Baswedan** (former Jakarta governor) and **Ganjar Pranowo** (former Central Java governor).
- His running mate was **Gibran Rakabuming Raka**, the eldest son of then-President Joko Widodo (Jokowi).
- Notably, this was Prabowo's third attempt at the presidency — he had previously lost to Joko Widodo in 2014 and 2019.
- Prabowo was inaugurated as Indonesia's **8th president on October 20, 2024**, succeeding Joko Widodo after his two-term limit ended.

2024-02-office-rnc.r:
No, Ronna McDaniel is no longer the chair of the Republican National Committee. She stepped down in March 2024 after announcing her intention to resign following pressure within the party, particularly after Donald Trump publicly backed a change in leadership.

She was succeeded by **Michael Whatley**, who had previously served as the chairman of the North Carolina Republican Party. He was formally elected as RNC Chair at the RNC's meeting in Houston on March 8, 2024. At the same time, **Lara Trump** (Donald Trump's daughter-in-law) was elected to serve as the committee's co-chair.

2024-03-death-carmen.r:
Eric Carmen died on **March 9, 2024**, at his home in Lyndhurst, Ohio. He was 74 years old.

His death was announced by his wife, Amy, and it was later reported that he died of idiopathic ventricular fibrillation, with coronary artery disease listed as a contributing factor.

Carmen was best known for hits like "All By Myself" (1975), "Hungry Eyes" (from *Dirty Dancing*), and "Make Me Lose Control," as well as being a founding member of the Raspberries, whose hit "Go All the Way" was a major power-pop classic.

2024-03-death-kahneman.r:
Daniel Kahneman has died. He passed away on **March 27, 2024**, at the age of 90.

Kahneman was born on March 5, 1934, in Tel Aviv (then part of British Mandate Palestine). He was awarded the 2002 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences for his pioneering work—much of it conducted with his longtime collaborator Amos Tversky—on judgment, decision-making, and prospect theory, which laid the foundation for modern behavioral economics. His best-selling book *Thinking, Fast and Slow* (2011) brought his research on cognitive biases and the two systems of thinking to a broad audience.

2024-03-death-gossett.r:
Louis Gossett Jr. has passed away. He died on **March 29, 2024**, at the age of 87, in Santa Monica, California. According to his death certificate, the cause was chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), along with heart failure and atrial fibrillation.

Gossett Jr. was a celebrated actor best known for:
- Winning the **Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor** for his role as Gunnery Sergeant Emil Foley in *An Officer and a Gentleman* (1982) — making him the first Black man to win in that category
- Winning an **Emmy Award** for his portrayal of Fiddler in the landmark miniseries *Roots* (1977)
- Other notable roles in films like *Iron Eagle*, *Enemy Mine*, and *A Soldier's Story*

2024-03-death-walsh.r:
M. Emmet Walsh has died. He passed away on **March 19, 2024**, at a hospital in St. Albans, Vermont, at the age of 88 — just three days shy of his 89th birthday. His death was attributed to cardiac arrest.

Walsh was a prolific character actor with a career spanning more than five decades and over 200 film and television credits. Beyond *Blade Runner* (1982), where he played Captain Bryant, and *Blood Simple* (1984), where he played the sleazy private detective Loren Visser, he was known for roles in *The Jerk*, *Fletch*, *Raising Arizona*, *My Best Friend's Wedding*, *Christmas with the Kranks*, and *Knives Out* (2019), among many others.

2024-03-death-mortensen.r:
Chris Mortensen has died. The longtime ESPN NFL reporter passed away on **March 24, 2024**, at the age of 72. ESPN announced his death that day.

Mortensen had been battling cancer — he was diagnosed with stage IV throat cancer in January 2016, went through treatment, and later returned to reporting after going into remission. He spent more than three decades at ESPN, joining the network in 1996, and was widely respected as one of the most prominent NFL journalists in the industry, known for breaking major stories and for his deep relationships across football.

2024-03-death-toriyama.r:
Akira Toriyama has passed away. He died on **March 1, 2024**, at the age of 68, due to an acute subdural hematoma (a buildup of blood between the skull and brain). His death was publicly announced on March 8, 2024, by his studio, Bird Studio, and Capsule Corporation Tokyo.

Toriyama was the legendary manga artist behind *Dragon Ball*, *Dr. Slump*, and the character designs for the *Dragon Quest* video game series and *Chrono Trigger*. His death prompted widespread tributes from fans and creators around the world.

2024-03-office-ireland.r:
Leo Varadkar stepped aside from both roles. On 20 March 2024, he announced his resignation as Taoiseach and as leader of Fine Gael, citing "personal and political" reasons and stating that he was no longer the best person for the job. He remained in a caretaker capacity until a successor was chosen.

Simon Harris was elected unopposed as Fine Gael leader on 24 March 2024 and succeeded Varadkar as Taoiseach on 9 April 2024, becoming Ireland's youngest-ever Taoiseach at age 37. Varadkar continued to serve as a TD (Teachta Dála) for Dublin West after stepping down from the leadership roles.

So, to summarize: Varadkar's tenure as Taoiseach (his second stint, which began in December 2022 under t…

2024-03-office-senegal.r:
Senegal's most recent presidential election took place on March 24, 2024. **Bassirou Diomaye Faye** won the election in the first round, securing roughly 54% of the vote and defeating Amadou Ba, the candidate backed by then-incumbent President Macky Sall. Faye thus became Senegal's president-elect and was inaugurated on April 2, 2024, making him the country's youngest-ever president at age 44.

Faye ran as an opposition candidate after his ally Ousmane Sonko was disqualified from contesting the election. His victory marked a significant political shift for Senegal, one of West Africa's most stable democracies.

2024-03-office-rnc.r: Michael Whatley was elected chair of the Republican National Committee on March 8, 2024, succeeding Ronna McDaniel. At the time of his election, Whatley was serving as chairman of the North Carolina Republican Party and had also worked as the RNC's general counsel. His election came after McDaniel announced her intention to step down following pressure from Donald Trump. Alongside Whatley, Lara Trump (the former president's daughter-in-law) was elected to serve as co-chair of the committee during the same vote in Houston.

2024-04-death-anderson.r: Terry Anderson is dead. The former Associated Press correspondent — who was the longest-held American hostage in Lebanon's civil war, held for nearly seven years (March 1985 to December 1991) after being abducted in West Beirut — died on **April 21, 2024**, at his home in Greenwood Lake, New York. He was 76 years old. His death followed a battle with prostate cancer, which he had publicly disclosed earlier that year.

2024-04-death-betts.r:
Dickey Betts is dead. He died on **April 18, 2024**, at his home in Osprey, Florida, at the age of 80.

His family announced that he passed away peacefully, surrounded by loved ones. In the period leading up to his death, he had been dealing with health problems, including chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and other chronic illnesses, as well as recovering from a head injury he suffered in a fall the previous year.

Betts was a founding member of the Allman Brothers Band and one of its lead guitarists, celebrated for his songwriting and playing on classics like "Ramblin' Man," "Blue Sky," and "In Memory of Elizabeth Reed."

2024-04-death-cavalli.r:
Roberto Cavalli is dead. The Italian fashion designer died on **April 12, 2024**, at his home in Florence, Italy, at the age of 83. His death was announced by the fashion house he founded, with reports indicating he had been suffering from a prolonged illness.

Cavalli was born on November 15, 1940, in Florence, and became famous for his glamorous, animal-print-heavy designs and his pioneering use of techniques like printing on leather and sand-blasted denim.

2024-04-death-higgs.r:
Peter Higgs is dead. He died on **8 April 2024**, at the age of 94, at his home in Edinburgh, Scotland. His death was announced by the University of Edinburgh on 10 April 2024.

Higgs (born 29 May 1929 in Newcastle upon Tyne) was a theoretical physicist at the University of Edinburgh who, in 1964, proposed the mechanism by which particles acquire mass — now known as the Higgs mechanism — and predicted the existence of the Higgs boson. The particle was finally discovered at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012, and Higgs shared the 2013 Nobel Prize in Physics with François Englert for the theoretical work.

2024-04-death-graham.r:
Former Florida governor and U.S. Senator Bob Graham is dead. He died on **April 16, 2024**, at the age of 87, in Gainesville, Florida.

Graham (born November 9, 1936) served as governor of Florida from 1979 to 1987 and represented Florida in the U.S. Senate from 1987 to 2005. He was known for his "workdays," in which he spent days doing ordinary jobs alongside workers, and for chairing the Senate Intelligence Committee and co-chairing the congressional inquiry into the September 11 attacks.

2024-04-death-simpson.r:
O.J. Simpson has died. He passed away on **April 10, 2024**, at the age of 76, in Las Vegas, Nevada. His death was announced by his family the following day via a post on X (formerly Twitter). He had been battling prostate cancer, which was the cause of his death.

Simpson was a Hall of Fame NFL running back and actor, but he was best known for his 1995 criminal trial, in which he was acquitted of the murders of his ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend Ron Goldman. He was later found liable for the deaths in a 1997 civil trial. In 2008, he was convicted of armed robbery and kidnapping in Las Vegas and served about nine years in prison before being released on parole in 2017.

2024-03-office-haiti.r:
Ariel Henry is no longer prime minister of Haiti — he resigned in March 2024 after months of mounting pressure.

Here's what happened:

- **Background:** Henry had served as acting prime minister (and effectively head of state) since July 2021, following the assassination of President Jovenel Moïse. He repeatedly postponed elections that were due by early 2024, extending his rule without a popular mandate.

- **Crisis:** In late February and early March 2024, powerful armed gangs launched coordinated attacks across Port-au-Prince, storming prisons, freeing thousands of inmates, attacking the airport, and explicitly demanding Henry's resignation. Henry was stranded outside the country (visiti…

2024-04-office-ireland.r:
Following Leo Varadkar's surprise resignation announcement in March 2024, **Simon Harris** succeeded him as Taoiseach. Harris, then the leader of Fine Gael, was appointed Taoiseach on 9 April 2024, becoming the youngest person ever to hold the office at age 37.

However, it's worth noting that after the general election held in November 2024, a new coalition government was formed, and **Micheál Martin** of Fianna Fáil returned as Taoiseach in January 2025 (he had previously served in the role from 2020 to 2022 under the rotating arrangement). Simon Harris became Tánaiste (deputy prime minister) in that government.

2024-03-death-lieberman.r:
Former U.S. Senator Joe Lieberman has died. He passed away on **March 27, 2024**, at the age of 82, in New York City. His death resulted from complications from a fall he suffered at his home, which caused a head injury.

Lieberman represented Connecticut in the Senate from 1989 to 2013 and was the Democratic Party's nominee for Vice President in the 2000 election as Al Gore's running mate. He later became an Independent and was known for his work on national security issues and his role in helping pass the Affordable Care Act.

2024-04-office-scotland.r: No. Humza Yousaf stepped down as First Minister of Scotland in May 2024. He announced his resignation in April 2024 after ending the SNP's power-sharing agreement with the Scottish Greens (the Bute House Agreement), which triggered a vote of no confidence against him. He was succeeded by John Swinney, who became First Minister on 7 May 2024.

2024-04-office-senegal.r:
Bassirou Diomaye Faye is the president of Senegal following the 2024 election. He won the presidential election held in March 2024, defeating Amadou Ba, the candidate backed by outgoing President Macky Sall's coalition. Faye took office on April 2, 2024, becoming Africa's youngest democratically elected leader at the time, at age 44.

Faye ran as the candidate of PASTEF (Patriots of Senegal for Work, Ethics, and Fraternity), the party founded by Ousmane Sonko, who subsequently became prime minister under Faye's administration. Notably, Faye had been released from prison just days before the election, having been detained on charges widely viewed by his supporters as politically motivated.

2024-05-death-hill.r:
Bernard Hill has died. He passed away on **May 5, 2024**, at the age of 79.

Hill was born on December 17, 1944, in Manchester, England. He was best known for:

- **King Théoden** in *The Lord of the Rings* film trilogy (2002–2003)
- **Captain Edward Smith** in *Titanic* (1997)
- **Yosser Hughes** in the acclaimed BBC drama *Boys from the Blackstuff* (1982)

His death was confirmed by his agent, Lou Coulson, though no cause of death was publicly disclosed. At the time of his passing, he had reportedly been preparing to begin work on a second series of the BBC drama *The Responder*, co-starring Martin Freeman.

2024-04-office-vietnam.r: No. Vương Đình Huệ stepped down from the position on April 26, 2024, when he resigned as Chairman of the National Assembly and lost his seats in the National Assembly and the Politburo. His resignation came amid Vietnam's ongoing anti-corruption campaign ("blazing furnace"), shortly after two of his assistants were arrested, with authorities citing violations of Party regulations. He was succeeded by Trần Thanh Mẫn, who was elected Chairman of the National Assembly on May 20, 2024.

2024-05-death-murray.r:
Grayson Murray has died. He passed away on **May 25, 2024**, at the age of **30**.

Murray, an American PGA Tour golfer born on October 1, 1993, in Raleigh, North Carolina, died by suicide. His death came one day after he withdrew from the Charles Schwab Challenge at Colonial Country Club in Fort Worth, Texas. He had been open about his long struggles with mental health and alcoholism, and his death prompted widespread discussion within the golf community about mental health awareness. He had won the Sony Open in Hawaii earlier that same year, in January 2024.

2024-05-death-albini.r:
Steve Albini has died. He passed away on **May 7, 2024**, at the age of 61, after suffering a **heart attack** at his home in Chicago. According to reports, he collapsed while working on a project with his Shellac bandmate Bob Weston, who was present at the time.

His death was announced by his bandmates in Shellac through the label Touch and Go Records. Albini was widely known as the frontman of bands like Big Black, Rapeman, and Shellac, and as one of the most respected recording engineers in rock music, having worked on thousands of albums — most famously Nirvana's *In Utero* — often refusing producer royalties as a matter of principle.

2024-04-office-paramount.r:
No, Bob Bakish is no longer the chief executive of Paramount Global. He stepped down as CEO in late April 2024, resigning amid the company's contentious merger negotiations with Skydance Media.

His role was not immediately filled by a single successor. Instead, Paramount replaced him with a three-person **"Office of the CEO"**, consisting of:

- **George Cheeks** – President and CEO of CBS
- **Chris McCarthy** – President and CEO of Showtime/MTV Entertainment Studios
- **Brian Robbins** – President and CEO of Paramount Pictures

These three executives served as co-CEOs, jointly running the company while the Skydance transaction moved forward.

Subsequently, once the Skydance–Paramount merge…

2024-05-office-peloton.r: John Foley stepped down as chief executive officer of Peloton in February 2022, amid a major restructuring that included plans to cut roughly 2,800 jobs (about 20% of its workforce). Foley, who co-founded the connected-fitness company, transitioned to the role of executive chairman. Barry McCarthy, a former executive at Spotify and Netflix, was named as his replacement as CEO.

2024-05-death-colin.r:
Charlie Colin has died. He passed away in **May 2025** at the age of 58.

Colin, who co-founded Train in San Francisco in the early 1990s and played bass on hits like "Meet Virginia" and "Drops of Jupiter," was found dead in an apartment in **Brussels, Belgium**, where he had been living and working as a music mentor/teacher. According to reports from his family, he had been house-sitting for a friend and is believed to have slipped and fallen in the shower; he was found after friends were unable to reach him for several days. News of his death became public around May 21–22, 2025.

Colin had left Train in the early 2000s (around 2003–2004) but remained active in music afterward, working as …

2024-05-office-scotland.r:
As of my knowledge cutoff in early 2025, the First Minister of Scotland is **John Swinney**. He took office in May 2024, succeeding Humza Yousaf, who resigned after just over a year in the role. Swinney is the leader of the Scottish National Party (SNP).

He is the seventh person to hold the office since devolution in 1999. Previous First Ministers include Donald Dewar, Henry McLeish, Jack McConnell, Alex Salmond, Nicola Sturgeon, and Humza Yousaf.

Please note that this information may have changed since my knowledge cutoff, so it's worth verifying with a current source if you need the latest information.

2024-05-death-walton.r:
Bill Walton has died. He passed away on **May 27, 2024**, at his home in San Diego, California, at the age of 71. His death followed a prolonged battle with cancer.

Walton was a legendary figure in basketball: a UCLA star under coach Jerry West-era basketball greats, MVP of the NBA championship-winning Portland Trail Blazers team in 1977, and later a beloved and famously colorful sports broadcaster for ESPN and other networks. His death prompted an outpouring of tributes from across the sports world.

2024-05-office-solomon.r: **Jeremiah Manele** was elected Prime Minister of the Solomon Islands, succeeding Manasseh Sogavare. This occurred on May 2, 2024, when Solomon Islands' parliament voted following the country's general election held in April 2024. Manele, a former foreign minister under Sogavare's government, led the Our Party coalition to victory and was chosen by lawmakers over opposition candidate Matthew Wale.

2024-05-office-macedonia.r:
**Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova** became the first female president of North Macedonia. She was elected in May 2024, defeating the incumbent president Stevo Pendarovski in the second round of voting with roughly 65% of the vote, and took office on May 12, 2024.

A law professor by background, she ran as the candidate of the VMRO-DPMNE party. Her election marked a historic milestone for the country, which had never previously been led by a woman since gaining independence from Yugoslavia in 1991.

2024-05-office-vietnam.r:
**Tô Lâm** was elected President of Vietnam following the resignation of Võ Văn Thưởng.

Võ Văn Thưởng resigned on March 20, 2024, amid allegations of violations and shortcomings (tied to the Communist Party's anti-corruption campaign), after serving only about a year in office. On May 22, 2024, the National Assembly elected Tô Lâm, who had been serving as Minister of Public Security, as the new President.

Notably, Tô Lâm's tenure was also relatively short in that role — after General Secretary Nguyễn Phú Trọng died in July 2024, Tô Lâm was chosen as General Secretary of the Communist Party in August 2024, and Lương Cường was subsequently elected President in October 2024.

2024-05-death-raisi.r:
**Ebrahim Raisi has died.**

He was killed on **May 19, 2024**, when the helicopter he was traveling in crashed in a mountainous, fog-shrouded area of **East Azerbaijan Province in northwestern Iran**, near the village of Uzi in the Varzaqan region, close to the border with Azerbaijan.

Key details:

- **Circumstances:** Raisi was returning from a ceremony inaugurating the Qiz Qalasi Dam on the Iran–Azerbaijan border, attended alongside Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev. The helicopter went down amid heavy fog and difficult terrain.
- **Others killed:** All eight people aboard died, including Iranian Foreign Minister **Hossein Amir-Abdollahian**, East Azerbaijan Governor Malek Rahmati, and …

2024-06-death-mull.r:
Martin Mull has died. He passed away on **June 27, 2024**, at his home in Los Angeles, at the age of 80. His death was announced by his daughter, writer Maggie Mull, who said he died after a long illness.

Mull was known for his deadpan comedic style and for roles in shows such as *Fernwood 2 Night*, *Roseanne* (as Leon Carp), *Sabrina the Teenage Witch* (as Principal Kraft), *Arrested Development* (as private investigator Gene Parmesan), and *Veep*. He was also an accomplished painter and musician.

2024-06-death-cobbs.r:
Bill Cobbs has died. The veteran character actor passed away on **June 25, 2024**, at his home in the Riverside, California area. He was 90 years old (he had celebrated his 90th birthday just days earlier, on June 16).

His death was announced by his brother, Thomas G. Cobbs, who shared the news in a Facebook post.

Bill Cobbs was known for a remarkably long career spanning decades, with memorable roles in films such as *Night at the Museum*, *The Bodyguard*, *Air Bud*, *Demolition Man*, *That Thing You Do!*, and *New Jack City*, as well as numerous television appearances on shows like *The Sopranos*, *ER*, *The West Wing*, and *General Hospital*.

2024-06-death-aimee.r:
Anouk Aimée has died. The French actress, best known for her roles in *A Man and a Woman* (1966), Federico Fellini's *La Dolce Vita* and *8½*, and Jacques Demy's *Lola* (1961), passed away on **June 18, 2024**, at her home in Paris. She was 92 years old — just weeks shy of what would have been her 93rd birthday (April 27).

Her death was announced by her family, and tributes poured in from across the French film world. She had remained active late in life, appearing in Claude Lelouch's *The Best Years of a Life* (*Les plus belles années d'une vie*, 2019), a sequel to *A Man and a Woman*. Over her career spanning more than seven decades, she earned an Oscar nomination for *A Man and a Woman* …

2024-06-death-sutherland.r:
Actor Donald Sutherland has died. He passed away on **June 20, 2024**, in Miami, Florida, at the age of 88. His son, actor Kiefer Sutherland, announced his father's death, stating that he had died after a long illness.

Donald Sutherland (born July 17, 1935, in Saint John, New Brunswick, Canada) had one of the longest and most distinguished careers in film, appearing in more than 200 movies over six decades. Some of his most notable films include *M\*A\*S\*H* (1970), *Klute* (1971), *Don't Look Now* (1973), *Invasion of the Body Snatchers* (1978), *Ordinary People* (1980), *JFK* (1991), and *The Hunger Games* series (2012–2015).

2024-06-death-mays.r:
Willie Mays has died. The baseball legend passed away on **June 18, 2024**, at the age of 93. According to his family's announcement, he died peacefully, surrounded by loved ones.

Mays, nicknamed the "Say Hey Kid," was widely regarded as one of the greatest baseball players of all time. He played primarily for the New York/San Francisco Giants over a career spanning more than 20 years, amassing 660 home runs and winning numerous honors, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2015.

His death came just days before he was scheduled to be honored by Major League Baseball in Birmingham, Alabama—the city where he grew up—prompting widespread tributes across the sports world.

2024-06-death-west.r:
Basketball Hall of Famer Jerry West has died. He passed away on **June 12, 2024**, at the age of 86. According to an announcement from the Los Angeles Clippers (where he had served as an executive advisor), he died peacefully with his wife, Karen, by his side.

West, nicknamed "Mr. Clutch" and often called "The Logo" because his silhouette inspired the NBA's logo, was born on May 30, 1938, in Chelyan, West Virginia. He was renowned as one of basketball's greatest players — a star athlete for the Los Angeles Lakers, a record-setting NBA Finals performer, and later a highly influential coach, manager, and executive who helped shape the careers of figures like Magic Johnson and Kobe Bryant.

2024-06-office-india.r:
Following the 2024 Indian general election, **Narendra Modi** was sworn in as Prime Minister of India on 9 June 2024, marking his third consecutive term in office.

However, his party, the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), did not win an outright majority on its own**. The BJP won 240 seats in the 543-member Lok Sabha, falling short of the 272 seats needed for a simple majority. This was a notable decline from the previous two elections (2014 and 2019), when the BJP had secured majorities on its own.

Despite this, Modi was able to form a government because the **National Democratic Alliance (NDA)** — the broader coalition led by the BJP — won a combined total of around 293 seats, securing a w…

2024-06-office-mexico.r:
Claudia Sheinbaum won Mexico's presidential election held on June 2, 2024, making her the first woman elected to lead the country in its history. She ran as the candidate of the ruling Morena party and its coalition allies, defeating Xóchitl Gálvez of the opposition coalition with roughly 60% of the vote.

Sheinbaum, a climate scientist and former mayor of Mexico City, took office on October 1, 2024, succeeding her political mentor, Andrés Manuel López Obrador.

2024-06-office-nato.r:
**Mark Rutte**, the former Prime Minister of the Netherlands, was selected to become the next Secretary General of NATO, succeeding Jens Stoltenberg.

Key details:
- Rutte emerged as the consensus candidate after other contenders withdrew their candidacies
- He was formally appointed by NATO leaders at the alliance's summit in Washington, D.C., in July 2024
- He officially took office on **October 1, 2024**
- He had served as Dutch Prime Minister for nearly 14 years (2010–2024), making him one of Europe's longest-serving leaders

Jens Stoltenberg, a former Norwegian Prime Minister, had held the post since 2014, with his tenure extended multiple times due to circumstances including Russia's f…

2024-07-death-duvall.r:
Shelley Duvall has died. She passed away on **July 11, 2024**, at her home in Blanco, Texas, at the age of 75. According to reports, she died in her sleep as a result of complications from diabetes.

Duvall was best known for her collaborations with director Robert Altman (including *McCabe & Mrs. Miller*, *Nashville*, and *3 Women*), her role as Wendy Torrance in Stanley Kubrick's *The Shining* (1980), and her portrayal of Olive Oyl in *Popeye* (1980). She also created and hosted children's programming such as *Faerie Tale Theatre*. After years away from acting, she returned to film late in life with a role in the 2023 horror film *The Forest Hills*.

2024-06-office-iceland.r:
**Halla Tómasdóttir** won Iceland's most recent presidential election, held on **June 1, 2024**.

Key details:
- She received roughly 34% of the vote in the first round, ahead of former Prime Minister **Katrín Jakobsdóttir** (~25%). Since no candidate won an outright majority, a runoff was expected, but Jakobsdóttir conceded shortly after the initial results, making Tómasdóttir president-elect.
- She took office on **August 1, 2024**, succeeding Guðni Th. Jóhannesson, who chose not to seek a third term.
- She is Iceland's seventh president since independence-era republican rule began in 1944, and the second woman to hold the office after Vigdís Finnbogadóttir.

Note that this reflects inform…

2024-06-office-southafrica.r:
**Cyril Ramaphosa was re-elected President of South Africa by the National Assembly on June 14, 2024**, following the general election held on May 29, 2024. He was elected unopposed after rival nominations fell through, receiving 283 votes.

**No, the ANC did not keep its parliamentary majority.** In a historic result, the African National Congress lost its outright majority for the first time since the end of apartheid in 1994. The ANC won roughly 40% of the vote, taking 159 of the 400 seats in the National Assembly—well short of the 201 seats needed for a majority.

As a result, Ramaphosa's ANC had to form a coalition government, known as the **Government of National Unity (GNU)**, which i…

2024-07-death-jacksonlee.r:
Sheila Jackson Lee has died. The Democratic U.S. Representative, who represented Texas's 18th Congressional District (covering much of Houston), passed away on **July 19, 2024**, at the age of 74.

She had announced in June 2024 that she had been diagnosed with pancreatic cancer. She died just weeks later, while she was actively campaigning for re-election in the November 2024 race. Following her death, former Houston Mayor Sylvester Turner won the November 2024 election to fill her seat, though he himself passed away in March 2025 shortly after taking office.

2024-07-death-jones.r:
Former NFL wide receiver and return specialist **Jacoby Jones has died**. He passed away on **July 14, 2024**, at his home in New Orleans, Louisiana. He was **40 years old** — he had turned 40 just three days earlier, on July 11, 2024.

According to the Orleans Parish coroner's report, his cause of death was **hypertensive cardiovascular disease**.

Jones was best known for his time with the Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens. He played a memorable role in the Ravens' Super Bowl XLVII victory, including a record-tying 108-yard kickoff return touchdown in that game and the famous "Mile High Miracle" catch against the Denver Broncos in the playoffs. After retiring as a player, he went into co…

2024-07-office-biden.r:
Joe Biden withdrew from the 2024 presidential race. On July 21, 2024, he announced that he would not seek reelection, ending his campaign roughly three weeks after a debate performance against Donald Trump that raised widespread concerns about his fitness for a second term and prompted calls from many fellow Democrats for him to step aside.

Shortly after withdrawing, Biden endorsed Vice President **Kamala Harris** to be the Democratic nominee. Harris secured the party's nomination at the Democratic National Convention in August 2024, selecting Minnesota Governor Tim Walz as her running mate. In the November 2024 general election, Donald Trump won the presidency, defeating Harris.

2024-07-death-mayall.r:
John Mayall has died. The British blues pioneer, often called the "Godfather of British Blues," passed away on **July 22, 2024**, at his home in California. He was 90 years old.

Mayall was born on November 29, 1933, in Macclesfield, Cheshire, England. His band, John Mayall & the Bluesbreakers, served as an incubator for some of rock music's greatest talents, including Eric Clapton, Peter Green, Mick Taylor, John McVie, and Mick Fleetwood.

Notably, shortly before his death it had been announced that he would receive the Musical Excellence Award at the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame's Class of 2024 induction ceremony, which took place later that year.

2024-07-death-haniyeh.r:
Ismail Haniyeh has died. He was assassinated on **July 31, 2024**, in **Tehran, Iran**.

Key details:

- **Circumstances**: Haniyeh, who led Hamas's political bureau from Doha, Qatar, was in Tehran to attend the inauguration of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian (held July 30, 2024). He was killed in an attack on the guesthouse/residence where he was staying.
- **Method**: Initial reports described a projectile or missile strike. Later reporting (notably by The New York Times) indicated he may have been killed by an explosive device that had been smuggled into his guesthouse roughly two months earlier and detonated remotely. Iranian authorities conducted an investigation into the breach of …

2024-07-office-starmer.r: **Keir Starmer** was appointed Prime Minister of the United Kingdom following the general election held on 4 July 2024. His Labour Party won a landslide victory, ending 14 years of Conservative-led government. Starmer was formally appointed by King Charles III and took office on 5 July 2024, succeeding Rishi Sunak, whose Conservative Party suffered its worst electoral result in its history.

2024-07-death-newhart.r:
Bob Newhart has died. He passed away on **July 18, 2024**, at his home in Los Angeles at the age of 94. His death followed a series of short illnesses, according to his longtime publicist.

Newhart was beloved for his deadpan comedic style and his signature one-sided telephone conversation routines. He rose to fame with his 1960 comedy album *The Button-Down Mind of Bob Newhart*, which won Grammy Awards, and later starred in two hit sitcoms: *The Bob Newhart Show* (1972–1978) and *Newhart* (1982–1990). He also appeared in films such as *Elf* (2003), playing Papa Elf, and made memorable guest appearances, including a recurring role on *The Big Bang Theory*.

2024-07-office-france.r:
**The New Popular Front (Nouveau Front Populaire)** — a left-wing alliance — won the most seats in France's snap legislative elections held on June 30 and July 7, 2024.

Key results:

1. **New Popular Front (left-wing coalition):** roughly 180–190 seats — the largest bloc
2. **Ensemble (President Macron's centrist alliance):** around 150–165 seats
3. **National Rally and allies (far right):** approximately 140–145 seats

However, no bloc came close to the 289 seats needed for an absolute majority, producing a **hung parliament**. The election had been called by President Emmanuel Macron after his alliance suffered heavy losses in the European Parliament elections, hoping to clarify the polit…

2024-07-office-pezeshkian.r:
**Masoud Pezeshkian**, a reformist politician and former health minister, won the snap presidential election held to replace Ebrahim Raisi, who died in a helicopter crash in May 2024.

Key details:
- The first round was held on June 28, 2024, but no candidate secured a majority, forcing a runoff.
- In the second round on July 5, 2024, Pezeshkian defeated hardline conservative candidate **Saeed Jalili**, winning roughly 54–55% of the vote.
- Pezeshkian, a heart surgeon and longtime member of parliament, positioned himself as a moderate reformist advocating for engagement with the West and easing social restrictions.
- He took office in July 2024, becoming Iran's ninth president since the 1979…

2024-08-death-delon.r:
Alain Delon has died. The French actor passed away on **August 18, 2024**, at his home in Douchy-Montcorbon, France. He was 88 years old.

His death was announced by his three children (Anthony, Anouchka, and Alain-Fabien Delon), who said he passed away peacefully, surrounded by family. In the years leading up to his death, his health had been declining — he suffered a stroke in 2019 and was later diagnosed with B-cell lymphoma, a type of cancer. There had also been a highly publicized family dispute over his medical care earlier in 2024.

Delon was one of the most iconic figures of French cinema, celebrated for films such as *Plein Soleil* (1960), *Rocco and His Brothers* (1960), *The Leopa…

2024-08-death-thorpe.r:
Graham Thorpe has died. The former England batsman passed away on **4 August 2024**, at the age of 55 — just three days after his birthday. His death was announced by Surrey Cricket Club, where he had spent much of his career as a player and later as a coach.

In September 2024, his family revealed that he had taken his own life, after suffering from depression and serious mental health issues for several years. His wife, Amanda, said he had been "incredibly unwell" in recent times despite appearing outwardly fine to many people.

Thorpe was one of England's most respected middle-order batsmen, playing from 1993 to 2005, and later served as England's associate director of batting before step…

2024-08-death-bean.r:
Billy Bean has died. He passed away on **August 6, 2024**, at the age of 60, after battling acute myeloid leukemia, a diagnosis he had publicly disclosed in 2023.

Billy Bean (born March 11, 1964, in Santa Ana, California) played Major League Baseball in the late 1980s and early 1990s for the Detroit Tigers, Los Angeles Dodgers, and San Diego Padres. After leaving baseball, he came out as gay in 1995, becoming one of the few openly gay former MLB players. He rejoined Major League Baseball in 2014 as its first Ambassador for Inclusion and later served as Vice President and Special Assistant to the CEO for Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging until his death.

Note: He should not be confused with …

2024-08-death-wojcicki.r:
Susan Wojcicki has died. She passed away on **August 9, 2024**, at the age of 56, after a battle with non-small cell lung cancer, which she had been fighting for roughly two years. Her death was announced by her husband, Dennis Troper.

For context on who she was:

- She was the CEO of YouTube from 2014 until February 2023, when she stepped down (Neal Mohan succeeded her).
- She was one of Google's earliest employees — famously renting out her garage in Menlo Park to Larry Page and Sergey Brin in 1998, which served as Google's first office.
- She later led the development of Google AdSense and oversaw Google's acquisition of YouTube in 2006 before becoming its CEO.

She is survived by her hu…

2024-07-death-simmons.r:
Richard Simmons has died. He passed away on **July 13, 2024**, at his home in the Hollywood Hills area of Los Angeles, one day after celebrating his 76th birthday. His longtime housekeeper found him unresponsive that morning, and he was pronounced dead at the scene.

**Cause of death:** The Los Angeles County Medical Examiner's office ruled the death to be from **natural causes**. According to the coroner's findings released afterward, the death was attributed to heart disease (atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease) along with complications from recent falls he had suffered in the months before his death.

- Simmons had been largely out of public view since around …

2024-08-office-menendez.r:
No, Bob Menendez is no longer a United States Senator. He resigned from the Senate on August 20, 2024, shortly after being convicted on federal corruption charges.

Here's a summary of what happened:

- **Conviction**: In July 2024, a federal jury convicted Menendez on 16 counts, including bribery, extortion, obstruction of justice, and acting as a foreign agent for Egypt. Prosecutors alleged he accepted bribes in the form of cash, gold bars, and a luxury car in exchange for using his political influence to benefit three New Jersey businessmen and the Egyptian government.

- **Resignation**: Following the conviction, Menendez initially resisted calls to resign but stepped down on August 20, …

2024-08-office-niccol.r: Brian Niccol, formerly the chairman and chief executive of Chipotle Mexican Grill, was named chairman and CEO of Starbucks, replacing Laxman Narasimhan. The announcement came in August 2024, with Niccol taking over in September 2024.

2024-08-office-paetongtarn.r:
Following the Constitutional Court's removal of Srettha Thavisin on August 14, 2024 (over an ethics violation related to a cabinet appointment), **Paetongtarn Shinawatra** became Prime Minister of Thailand. She was elected by Parliament on August 16, 2024, and is the daughter of former Prime Minister Thaksin Shinawatra and a leader of the Pheu Thai Party. At age 37, she became the youngest person ever to hold the office of Prime Minister in Thailand.

It's worth noting that Paetongtarn's own tenure was later cut short: she was suspended by the Constitutional Court in July 2025 pending an ethics case involving a leaked phone call with Cambodian leader Hun Sen, and she was removed from office …

2024-09-death-ashton.r:
John Ashton, the actor best known for playing Detective Sergeant John Taggart in the *Beverly Hills Cop* films, has died. He passed away on **September 26, 2024**, in Fort Collins, Colorado, at the age of 76. He had been battling cancer and died while in hospice care.

Notably, he had recently reprised his role as Taggart in *Beverly Hills Cop: Axel F*, which was released on Netflix in July 2024, just a couple of months before his death.

2024-08-death-fatman-scoop.r:
Fatman Scoop (born Isaac Freeman III) has died. He passed away on August 30, 2024, at the age of 53.

**Circumstances of his death:** He collapsed while performing on stage at Town Center Park in Hamden, Connecticut, during a free summer concert series event. Bystanders and emergency responders administered CPR at the scene, and he was rushed to a nearby hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

The Connecticut Office of the Chief Medical Examiner later ruled his death to be from natural causes, attributing it to hypertensive and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (i.e., heart disease).

His death was announced by his family and his booking agency shortly afterward, prompting an outpourin…

2024-08-office-yunus.r:
**Muhammad Yunus** leads Bangladesh's interim government as its Chief Adviser.

Following the fall of Sheikh Hasina's government on August 5, 2024 — after weeks of student-led protests that turned into a mass uprising — Hasina resigned and fled to India. On August 8, 2024, Nobel Peace Prize laureate and economist Muhammad Yunus was sworn in as Chief Adviser of the interim government, effectively serving as head of government. He was chosen through consultations involving student protest leaders, President Mohammed Shahabuddin, and military leadership. The interim government's mandate includes restoring stability, implementing reforms, and eventually organizing new elections.

2024-08-office-sinwar.r:
**Yahya Sinwar** was chosen to lead Hamas's political bureau after Ismail Haniyeh was assassinated in Tehran on July 31, 2024. Sinwar, who had been the head of Hamas in Gaza and was regarded as a key architect of the October 7, 2023 attack on Israel, was selected as Haniyeh's successor in early August 2024.

Sinwar himself was later killed by Israeli forces in mid-October 2024 in Rafah, Gaza. Following his death, Hamas reportedly did not immediately announce a permanent successor, with reports indicating that a council of senior officials would manage the group's affairs in the interim.

2024-08-office-hasina.r:
No, Sheikh Hasina is no longer the Prime Minister of Bangladesh. Here's what happened:

**Resignation and flight (August 2024):** After weeks of massive student-led protests—which began over a controversial government job quota system and escalated into a broader anti-government uprising—Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled the country on August 5, 2024. She traveled by helicopter to India, where she has remained in exile ever since. The protests and the government's crackdown left hundreds of people dead.

**Interim government:** Following her departure, an interim government was formed headed by Nobel Peace Prize laureate **Muhammad Yunus** as Chief Adviser, tasked with restoring order and prep…

2024-09-death-kristofferson.r:
Kris Kristofferson has died. He passed away on **September 28, 2024**, at his home in Maui, Hawaii, at the age of 88. His family announced his death the following day, though no specific cause was disclosed. In his later years, he had experienced memory problems, which were initially diagnosed as Alzheimer's disease but were later attributed to Lyme disease.

Kristofferson was a legendary figure in country music, known for writing classics like "Me and Bobby McGee," "Help Me Make It Through the Night," "Sunday Mornin' Comin' Down," and "For the Good Times." He was also a successful actor, starring in films such as *A Star Is Born* (1976), *Pat Garrett and Billy the Kid*, and the *Blade* tril…

2024-09-death-rose.r:
Pete Rose has died. He passed away on **September 30, 2024**, at his home in Las Vegas, Nevada. He was 83 years old.

According to the Clark County (Nevada) coroner's office, his cause of death was hypertensive and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease — meaning heart-related conditions involving high blood pressure and hardened/narrowed arteries. He was reportedly found unresponsive by a family member.

Rose held baseball's all-time hits record with 4,256 hits across his career, surpassing players like Ty Cobb. Despite that achievement, he spent decades barred from baseball after being banned in 1989 amid allegations that he gambled while managing baseball teams, which also kept him from b…

2024-09-death-jones.r:
James Earl Jones has died. He passed away on **September 9, 2024**, at his home in Pawling, New York. He was 93 years old.

Jones was born on January 17, 1931, and was one of the most celebrated actors of his generation, renowned for his commanding bass voice and stage presence. He was best known for:

- Voicing **Darth Vader** in the *Star Wars* films
- Voicing **Mufasa** in Disney's *The Lion King*
- His Oscar-nominated performance in *The Great White Hope* (1970)

2024-09-death-jackson.r:
Tito Jackson has died. He passed away on **September 15, 2024**, at the age of 70.

According to reports, he suffered an apparent heart attack while driving near Gallup, New Mexico, and died as a result. His death was announced by his sons (the members of the group 3T), who confirmed the news on September 16, 2024.

Tito Jackson (born Toriano Adaryll Jackson on October 15, 1953) was one of the founding members of the Jackson 5 alongside his brothers Jackie, Jermaine, Marlon, and Michael. He was known for playing guitar with the group throughout its history.

2024-09-death-smith.r:
Dame Maggie Smith has died. She passed away on **September 27, 2024**, at the age of 89, at Chelsea and Westminster Hospital in London. Her death was announced by her sons, actors Toby Stephens and Chris Larkin, who said she was surrounded by friends and family at the time.

She was one of Britain's most celebrated actresses, known for iconic roles such as Professor Minerva McGonagall in the *Harry Potter* films, Violet Crawley, Dowager Countess of Grantham in *Downton Abbey*, and her Oscar-winning performances in *The Prime of Miss Jean Brodie* (1969) and *California Suite* (1978).

2024-09-office-hill.r: Elliott Hill was named to become the chief executive officer of Nike, Inc., replacing John Donahoe. The announcement was made in September 2024, with Hill taking over as President and CEO effective October 14, 2024. Hill was a longtime Nike veteran who had spent over 30 years at the company before retiring in 2020. His return was seen as an effort to revitalize the company's culture and address challenges Nike faced under Donahoe's leadership, including declining sales and increased competition.

2024-09-office-barnier.r:
Emmanuel Macron appointed **Michel Barnier** as Prime Minister of France on 5 September 2024, succeeding Gabriel Attal. Barnier, a veteran center-right politician best known internationally for serving as the European Union's chief Brexit negotiator, became the first prime minister appointed following the July 2024 snap legislative elections that produced a hung parliament.

For added context: Barnier's tenure was short-lived. His government lost a no-confidence vote on 4 December 2024 over budget disputes, making it the shortest-lived French government of the Fifth Republic at that time. Macron then appointed **François Bayrou** as Prime Minister on 13 December 2024.

2024-09-death-nasrallah.r:

Key details:

- **Confirmation**: Israel announced his death on September 28, 2024, and Hezbollah subsequently confirmed that its longtime Secretary-General had been killed.
- **Others killed in the strike**: The attack also killed Ali Karaki, a senior Hezbollah commander res…

2024-09-office-dissanayake.r:
**Anura Kumara Dissanayake** won Sri Lanka's presidential election held on **September 21, 2024**, defeating the incumbent president, **Ranil Wickremesinghe**.

Key details:
- Dissanayake is the leader of the National People's Power (NPP) coalition and its main constituent party, the Marxist-leaning Janatha Vimukthi Peramuna (JVP).
- He initially led with about 42% of first-preference votes, and once second-preference votes were tallied (as required since no candidate exceeded 50%), he crossed the threshold needed to win outright.
- Wickremesinghe had been president since July 2022, when he was elected by Parliament following the resignation of Gotabaya Rajapaksa amid mass protests over Sri …

2024-10-death-garr.r:
Actress Teri Garr has died. She passed away on **October 29, 2024**, at her home in Los Angeles at the age of 79.

Garr had been living with multiple sclerosis, which she was diagnosed with in the late 1990s and publicly disclosed in 2002. She became an advocate for MS awareness after her diagnosis.

Known for her comedic roles in films like *Young Frankenstein* (1974), *Tootsie* (1982)—for which she received an Academy Award nomination—*Close Encounters of the Third Kind* (1977), and *Mr. Mom* (1983), Garr was widely regarded as one of Hollywood's most beloved comic actresses. Her death was confirmed by her daughter, Molly O'Meara Meeks.

2024-10-death-lesh.r:
Phil Lesh has died. He passed away on **October 25, 2024**, at the age of 84. His death was announced by his family, who said he died peacefully and "surrounded by full of love and his family." A specific cause of death was not publicly disclosed, though he had a well-documented history of health issues over the years, including bladder cancer (diagnosed in 1998), prostate cancer, and a liver transplant in 1998.

Lesh was a founding member of the Grateful Dead in 1965 and served as the band's bassist until its dissolution following Jerry Garcia's death in 1995. He continued performing for decades afterward, most notably with his band Phil Lesh and Friends, and remained active in the music sc…

2024-10-death-tata.r:
Ratan Tata has died. He passed away on **October 9, 2024**, at Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai, India, at the age of 86. He had been admitted to the hospital a few days earlier due to age-related health issues and elevated blood pressure.

His death prompted an outpouring of tributes across India and internationally, and he was accorded a state funeral in Mumbai. Ratan Tata had served as chairman of Tata Sons from 1991 to 2012, and briefly returned as interim chairman from 2016 to 2017. He was widely respected for his business leadership and philanthropy, including his work through the Tata Trusts.

2024-10-death-gaynor.r:
As far as I know, **Mitzi Gaynor is alive**. Born on September 4, 1931, in Chicago, the star of *South Pacific* (1958) — where she played Ensign Nellie Forbush — has not been reported dead as of my knowledge cutoff in early 2025. That would make her in her early nineties.

She remained active in later years through interviews, appearances at classic film events, and the 2008 documentary about her television specials, *Mitzi Gaynor: Razzle Dazzle! The Special Years*.

One caveat: since she is quite elderly, if you're checking for very recent news, I'd recommend verifying with a current source, as anything that happened after my knowledge cutoff wouldn't be reflected in my answer.

2024-10-death-salmond.r: Alex Salmond has died. The former First Minister of Scotland passed away on **12 October 2024**, at the age of 69. He collapsed shortly after delivering a speech at a conference in Ohrid, North Macedonia, and could not be revived. His death came as a shock to many in Scottish politics, where he had been a dominant figure for decades — serving as First Minister from 2007 to 2014 and leading the SNP through the 2014 independence referendum.

2024-10-death-sinwar.r:

- **Final moments:** Drone footage released by the IDF showed Sinwar, visibly wounded and covered in dust, seated in a damaged chair inside a destroyed building. In his final moments, he threw a stick at the drone hovering nearby.
- **Cause of death:** Reports indicated he died from a gunshot…

Hill is a company veteran with over 30 years of experience at Nike before his retirement in 2020, and he returned to lead the company amid efforts to revitalize its business and address declining sales.

**How he died:** He fell from a third-floor balcony at the CasaSur Palermo Hotel in Buenos Aires, Argentina. He was pronounced dead at the scene due to multiple traumatic injuries consistent with the fall.

**Circumstances:** In the moments before his death, hotel staff had called emergency services reporting that a guest was behaving erratically and possibly under the influence of drugs or alcohol. An autopsy later detected multiple substances in his system, including traces of what is sometimes referred to as "pink cocaine" (a drug cocktail), along with alcohol and other substances. 2024-10-death-valenzuela.r:
Fernando Valenzuela has died. The legendary Mexican-born pitcher — famous for "Fernandomania" in 1981, when he won both the Rookie of the Year and Cy Young awards while helping the Dodgers win the World Series — passed away on **October 22, 2024**, at the age of 63.

His death came just days before the Dodgers clinched the 2024 World Series title, making the moment bittersweet for fans. He had reportedly been hospitalized in the weeks leading up to his death. Valenzuela remained closely tied to the Dodgers throughout his life, serving for years as a Spanish-language broadcaster for the team's broadcasts.

- The coalition fell from 279 seats to roughly **215 seats** (about 191 for the LDP and 24 for Komeito) — well below the **233 seats** needed for a majority in the 465-seat chamber.
- This was the first time since 2009 that the LDP-led coalition failed to win a majority in a general election.
- Key factors included public anger over the LDP's political funds scandal ("slush fund" affair), inflation, and the party's poor standing among younger voters.

2024-11-death-quincy-jones.r:
Quincy Jones has died. He passed away on **November 3, 2024**, at his home in Bel Air, Los Angeles, at the age of 91. According to his publicist, he died peacefully, surrounded by his family.

Quincy Jones was one of the most influential figures in American music history — a producer, composer, and arranger best known for producing Michael Jackson's *Thriller* (the best-selling album of all time), his work with Frank Sinatra, co-producing "We Are the World," and composing scores for films and television, among many other accomplishments over a career spanning more than seven decades.

2024-11-death-jamison.r:
Judith Jamison has died. She passed away on **November 9, 2024**, in New York City at the age of 81, following a brief illness. Her death was announced by the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, which she had led as artistic director from 1989 to 2011.

Jamison was one of the most celebrated figures in American dance. She joined the Alvin Ailey company in 1965 and became world-renowned for her performance in "Cry" (1971), the iconic 16-minute solo that Alvin Ailey choreographed for her as a tribute to Black women. After Ailey's death in 1989, she succeeded him as artistic director and guided the company for over two decades, becoming only the second person to hold that role.

- In October 2024, he gained public attention as a whistleblower when he told the New York Times that he believed OpenAI's use of copyrighted material to train ChatGPT did not qualify as fair use under U.S. copyright law.
- His death came shortly before he was expected to be deposed as a witness in copyright infringement lawsuits against OpenAI, including one filed by the New York Times.

Key details:
- Ishiba won the Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) leadership election on **September 27, 2024**, defeating Sanae Takaichi in a runoff vote.
- He was formally elected as Prime Minister by the National Diet on **October 1, 2024**, becoming Japan's 102nd prime minister.
- Ishiba, a former defense minister, had previously run for the LDP leadership several times unsuccessfully before finally winning in 2024.
- Kishida had announced in August 2024 that he would step down and not seek re-election as party leader, amid declining approval ratings and a political fundraising scandal within the LDP.

2024-11-death-bradford.r:
Barbara Taylor Bradford has died. The British-born novelist, best known for her 1979 blockbuster *A Woman of Substance*, passed away on **November 24, 2024**, at her home in New York City. She was 91 years old (she was born on May 10, 1933, in Leeds, England).

Her death followed a short illness, according to reports at the time. Over her career, she wrote more than 40 novels, selling tens of millions of copies worldwide, with *A Woman of Substance* — the saga of Emma Harte's rise from servant girl to business empire — remaining her signature work and spawning numerous sequels and television adaptations.

2024-11-death-west.r:
Timothy West has died. The British actor passed away on **12 November 2024**, at the age of 90. He died peacefully in his sleep at a care home in London, according to announcements made by his family, including his son, the actor Samuel West.

West had a long and distinguished career spanning more than six decades, known for his stage work (including acclaimed performances as King Lear), television roles such as playing Winston Churchill, and his appearances alongside his wife Prunella Scales in the travel series *Great Canal Journeys*.

2024-11-office-trump-election.r:
Donald Trump won the most recent U.S. presidential election, held on November 5, 2024. He defeated Kamala Harris, the sitting Vice President who became the Democratic nominee after President Joe Biden withdrew from the race in July 2024.

Trump won 312 electoral votes compared to Harris's 226, and he carried all seven of the key battleground states. His victory made him the 47th president of the United States, and he was inaugurated on January 20, 2025. Notably, this marked a second, non-consecutive term for Trump, who had previously served as the 45th president from 2017 to 2021.

2024-11-office-gaetz.r:
President-elect Donald Trump's first nominee for U.S. Attorney General was **Matt Gaetz**, a former Republican congressman from Florida. Trump announced Gaetz's nomination on November 13, 2024.

However, **Gaetz did not go on to hold the office**. Just over a week later, on November 21, 2024, he withdrew his name from consideration amid scrutiny over a House Ethics Committee investigation into allegations of misconduct (he has denied wrongdoing).

Following Gaetz's withdrawal, Trump quickly nominated **Pam Bondi**, a former Florida attorney general and longtime Trump ally. Bondi was confirmed by the Senate on February 4, 2025, and she went on to serve as U.S. Attorney General.

2024-12-death-carter.r:
Former U.S. President Jimmy Carter has died. He passed away on **December 29, 2024**, at his home in Plains, Georgia, at the age of 100.

Some context:
- He was the longest-lived president in U.S. history and the first to reach his 100th birthday (October 1, 2024).
- He had been in hospice care since February 2023.
- His wife of 77 years, Rosalynn Carter, predeceased him, dying in November 2023.
- He served as the 39th president from 1977 to 1981 and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2002 for his humanitarian work.

2024-11-office-hegseth.r:
President-elect Donald Trump nominated **Pete Hegseth** to serve as U.S. Secretary of Defense in November 2024, following his victory in the 2024 presidential election.

Hegseth is a former Fox News host (co-host of *Fox & Friends Weekend*) and an Army National Guard veteran who served tours in Iraq, Afghanistan, and at Guantanamo Bay. He was also an executive director of Vets for Freedom and Concerned Veterans for America, and authored several books, including *The War on Warriors*.

His nomination was notable because he was not a conventional choice for the role—he had no experience running a large organization like the Pentagon—and it drew significant scrutiny over questions about his qua…

Following Mauritius's most recent general election, held on 10 November 2024, **Navin Ramgoolam** became prime minister. He leads the Labour Party and headed the "Alliance du Changement" (Alliance for Change) coalition, which won a landslide victory, taking all 60 directly elected seats in the National Assembly.

He replaced **Pravind Jugnauth**, leader of the Militant Socialist Movement (MSM), who had served as prime minister since 2017 and whose coalition had governed since the 2019 election. Jugnauth conceded defeat shortly after the results were announced, and Ramgoolam was sworn in as prime minister on 13 November 2024 — marking his third stint in the role, having previously served as p…

2024-12-death-giovanni.r:
Nikki Giovanni, the celebrated American poet and a leading voice of the Black Arts Movement, has died. She passed away on **December 9, 2024**, at the age of 81, in Blacksburg, Virginia. Her death was due to complications from lung cancer, which she had first been diagnosed with decades earlier and which later recurred.

Born Yolande Cornelia Giovanni Jr. on June 7, 1943, in Knoxville, Tennessee, she was known for works such as *Black Feeling, Black Talk*, *Ego-Tripping*, and *Acolytes*. She was also a longtime professor at Virginia Tech and delivered the memorable "We are Virginia Tech" address after the 2007 campus shooting.

2024-12-death-henderson.r:
Rickey Henderson has died. The legendary Hall of Fame outfielder passed away on **December 20, 2024**, in Oakland, California, at the age of 65 — just five days shy of his 66th birthday. Reports indicated he had been battling health issues, including pneumonia following a fight with cancer.

Henderson is widely regarded as one of the greatest players in baseball history. Known as the "Man of Steal," he holds the MLB records for career stolen bases (1,406) and career runs scored (2,295), and he played for teams including the Oakland Athletics, New York Yankees, and Toronto Blue Jays over a career spanning from 1979 to 2003. He was inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 2009.

**The resignation:** On November 12, 2024, Welby announced he would step down. This followed the publication of the **Makin Review**, an independent investigation into the Church of England's handling of abuse committed by **John Smyth**, a barrister who physically and sexually abused more than 100 boys and young men connected to Christian summer camps in the UK, Zimbabwe, and South Africa. Sportscaster **Greg Gumbel has died**. He passed away in December 2024 at the age of 78. His death was announced on December 21, 2024, by his family, who said he died peacefully surrounded by loved ones after a battle with cancer. He had stepped away from his duties at CBS Sports earlier that year for health-related reasons.

Gumbel had a long and distinguished broadcasting career, best known for his decades of work with CBS Sports, where he anchored coverage of the NFL (including Super Bowl broadcasts), NCAA college basketball tournaments such as March Madness, and other major sporting events. He was also the older brother of journalist Bryant Gumbel.

- **Where:** Outside the New York Hilton Midtown hotel, where UnitedHealth Group was scheduled to hold its annual investor day.
- **How:** He was shot by a masked gunman who had been waiting for him. Thompson was struck in the back and leg and was pronounced dead at the scene. He was 50 years old.

Former Indian Prime Minister **Manmohan Singh has passed away**. He died on **December 26, 2024**, at the age of 92.

He was admitted to the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS) in New Delhi after experiencing a sudden loss of consciousness at home, and his condition deteriorated despite resuscitation efforts. Age-related health complications were cited as contributing factors.

Manmohan Singh served as India's 13th Prime Minister from 2004 to 2014, leading the United Progressive Alliance (UPA) government for two consecutive terms. Before that, he was widely credited as the architect of India's economic liberalization while serving as Finance Minister from 1991 to 1996 under Prime…

2025-01-death-faithfull.r:
Marianne Faithfull has died. The English singer and actress passed away on **January 30, 2025**, in London at the age of 78. According to announcements made by her spokesperson, she died peacefully in her sleep while surrounded by family.

Faithfull, born on December 29, 1946, had faced significant health challenges in her later years, including a battle with breast cancer, hepatitis C, and long COVID following an infection in 2020. She was best known for her 1960s hits like "As Tears Go By" and for later acclaimed work such as her landmark album *Broken English* (1979).

Christian Lindner was fired by Chancellor Olaf Scholz on November 6, 2024, which triggered the collapse of the three-party "traffic light" coalition (SPD, Greens, FDP).

**The dispute:** The conflict centered on Germany's constitutionally enshrined "debt brake" (*Schuldenbremse*), which strictly limits federal borrowing. Scholz wanted to relax or suspend it to allow tens of billions of euros in extra spending on defense, Ukraine aid, infrastructure, and economic stimulus. Lindner, a fiscal hawk and leader of the pro-market FDP, refused, insisting on strict adherence to the debt brake and demanding spending cuts instead.
